#### G3.13 — Sheep grazing fidelity · XS · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** `animation.sheep.grazing.v2`, `"animation_length": 2.0` — **40 ticks = 2.0 s**. The head **translates** as well as rotating: `head.position.y` goes 0 → `query.is_baby ? −2.5 : −9.0` over the first **0.2 s (4 ticks)**, holds until **1.8 s**, then returns over the last 0.2 s. So an adult sheep's head drops **9 units = 0.5625 blocks** to actually reach the grass. The rotation is `180 × (0.2 + 0.07 × sin(key_frame_lerp_time × 1644.39))` ⇒ a **36° base pitch with a ±12.6° nibble** at roughly **2.3 nibbles per second**. [https://github.com/Mojang/bedrock-samples/blob/main/resource_pack/animations/sheep.animation.json]
- **What we have:** `Creature.cpp:348–359`. `kGrazeSeconds = 1.8f` (against 2.0), `kGrazeHeadPitch = 0.7f` rad = **40.1°** (against 36°), `kGrazeChancePerSecond = 0.001f * 20`, baby `0.02f * 20`. It sets `targetHeadPitch` and nothing else — **no translation, no ramp, no nibble**. The head rotates down and hangs there. (Read in the code.)
- **What must be built:** Add a head translation term inside the existing `beginHead()` frame; add the 4-tick ramp in and out; add the nibble as a small sine on top of the base pitch. All three are inside one function.
- **Numbers that matter:** duration **40 ticks = 2.0 s**; head drop **9 units = 0.5625 blocks** adult, **2.5 units = 0.15625 blocks** baby; ramp **4 ticks = 0.2 s** in and out with a **32-tick = 1.6 s** hold; base pitch **36° = 0.6283 rad**; nibble **±12.6° = ±0.2199 rad** at **≈2.3 Hz**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** The head translation must be applied in the head's local frame *before* the rotation, or the head will swing on an arc instead of dropping. `beginHead`/`endHead` already establish that frame, so this is the cheap case. The baby figure needs `kBabyScale` awareness — and note the reference's baby drop is **not** simply `0.55 × 9`, it is an authored 2.5, so do not derive it.

#### G3.14 — Species-specific death · XS · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** Death lasts **20 ticks = 1.0 s**, after which the body vanishes with a burst of white smoke — **no fade, no shrink**. Most mobs fall onto their **left side**. **Spiders, cave spiders, silverfish and endermites flip upside-down** rather than sideways. **Squid have no death animation at all.** There is no `animation.*.death` in the 155-file animations directory — like the hurt tint, it is engine-side. The `[JE]` curve is `roll = min(sqrt(deathTime / 20 × 1.6), 1) × 90°` about the body's local Z, which reaches 90° at **12.5 ticks** and holds for the remaining 7.5. The `sqrt` makes it **front-loaded** — the body drops fast and settles. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Death]
- **What we have:** `Creature.cpp:62–64` and `:74–80`. `kDeathTipSeconds = 0.625f` = **12.5 ticks** ✅ and `kDeathSeconds = 1.0f` = 20 ticks ✅ — both exactly right. The easing is **smoothstep `t²(3−2t)`** where the reference is `sqrt` — ours is symmetric and eases *in*, the reference starts fast. And there is **one rule for all 57 species** (`:5297–5312`), a Rodrigues rotation about `{sinYaw, 0, cosYaw}`. (Read in the code.)
- **What must be built:** Replace the smoothstep with `min(sqrt(t × 1.6), 1)`. Add a `deathStyle` to `CreatureSpecies` with three values — `Side` (default), `Flip` (spider, cave spider, silverfish, voidmite), `None` (squid, glow squid). Check by eye which side ours falls onto and match the reference's left.
- **Numbers that matter:** tip **12.5 ticks = 0.625 s** to **90°**; total **20 ticks = 1.0 s**; curve `min(sqrt(t × 1.6), 1)` where `t = deathTime/20`. Flip species rotate **180°** about the forward axis, not 90°.
- **Risks / dependencies:** The render lift `halfWidth × scale × sin(fallAngle)` at `:5297–5312` is derived for a 90° side-fall; a 180° flip needs the box's *height* in that term instead, or an upside-down spider will sink into the floor. Derive the lift from the rotated bounding extent rather than special-casing it, or this becomes the "derivation applied to one of a pair and not the other" bug shape. **Whether we currently tip left or right needs a play check I could not perform.**

#### G3.15 — Item-entity fidelity · XS–S · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** `[JE]` `ItemEntityRenderer`, visually identical in Bedrock.
  - **Bob:** `sin((age + partialTick)/10 + bobOffs) × 0.1 + 0.1` ⇒ period **20π ≈ 62.83 ticks ≈ 3.142 s**, amplitude **0.1 block about a +0.1 offset**. It bobs **always**, in air, in water and on the ground.
  - **`bobOffs = random.nextFloat() × 2π`** — a **per-entity constant, assigned once at spawn**. This is what stops a pile of drops pulsing in unison.
  - **Spin:** `getSpin(partial) = (age + partial) / 20` radians ⇒ **0.05 rad/tick = 1.0 rad/s = 57.296°/s**, one revolution every **125.66 ticks ≈ 6.283 s**. (The wiki's "2.9°/tick" is a rounding error; the exact figure is 2.8648°/tick.)
  - **Stack multi-copy:** count > 1 → 2 copies, > 16 → 3, > 32 → 4, > 48 → 5. 3D block items offset each copy by `(rand × 2 − 1) × 0.15` on X, Y and Z; flat sprite items offset by **±0.075** on X and Y plus a fixed **+0.09375** Z step per copy so they stack like cards. The RNG is seeded from `Item.getId(item) + damage`, so **the same item always makes the same pile** — deliberate, and it stops the pile shimmering on reload.
  - Despawn is **6000 ticks = 5 minutes**.
  [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Item_(entity)]
- **What we have:** `ItemEntity.cpp:35–37` — `kBobHeight = 0.07f`, `kBobSpeed = 2.2f`, `kSpinSpeed = 1.1f`. Render at `:247–253`:
  ```
  bob  = drop.onGround ? (sin(timeSeconds * 2.2 + drop.position.x) * 0.5 + 0.5) * 0.07 : 0
  spin = timeSeconds * 1.1 + drop.position.z
  ```
  Bob period **2π/2.2 = 2.856 s** (against 3.142), amplitude 0.07 (against 0.1, and ours is 0→0.07 rather than ±0.1 about +0.1). Spin **1.1 rad/s** ⇒ **5.712 s/rev** (against 6.283). Despawn 5 min ✅. Single copy only. (Read in the code.)
- **What must be built:**
  1. **Seed the phase once.** Add `bobPhase` and `spinPhase` to the drop, set from a random value at spawn. See §3.4 #2 — deriving phase from live position is a real, visible bug, not a stylistic difference.
  2. **Remove the `onGround` gate** — bob always.
  3. Correct the constants to the reference's.
  4. Multi-copy by stack count, with the seeded-from-item-id RNG so it is stable.
- **Numbers that matter:** bob period **62.83 ticks = 3.1416 s** ⇒ rate **2.0 rad/s** (not 2.2); bob `sin(...) × 0.1 + 0.1` blocks; spin **1.0 rad/s** exactly (not 1.1) ⇒ **125.66 ticks = 6.2832 s** per revolution; copy thresholds **1 / 16 / 32 / 48**; 3D jitter **±0.15**, flat jitter **±0.075** with a **0.09375** Z step; despawn **6000 ticks = 300 s**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** None — `ItemEntity.cpp` is self-contained. Multi-copy multiplies the draw call count for large piles; cap by distance if it shows up in a frame-time probe (and per `CLAUDE.md`, measure before optimising).

#### G3.16 — Arrow shake axis and rest roll · XS · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** The arrow's flight orientation is `yaw = atan2(vx, vz)` and `pitch = atan2(vy, horizontalDistance)`, then smoothed toward the new heading by `lerpRotation` at factor **0.2** per tick. The renderer applies `YP(lerp(yRotO, yRot) − 90°)`, then `ZP(lerp(xRotO, xRot))`, then the shake as `ZP(−sin(shakeTime × 3) × shakeTime)` **in degrees, on roll**, and finally a **fixed `XP(45°)` roll** so the fletching sits diagonally rather than axis-aligned. Model scale 0.05625. `shakeTime = 7` on impact ⇒ **7 ticks = 0.35 s** of decaying wobble. Because the shake is on roll, an embedded arrow **quivers about its own shaft** and its direction never changes. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Arrow]
- **What we have:** `Projectile.cpp:147–370`. `kShakeSeconds = 0.35f` ✅ exactly right. But `:366–369` computes `wobble = −sin(shake × 10) × shake × 0.6` and applies it **to pitch**, which bends the heading — so an arrow stuck in a wall appears to be still steering, and one stuck in a creature waves. There is no fixed 45° rest roll. The prev→current heading blend at `:361` is correct and matches the reference's `lerpRotation`. (Read in the code.)
- **What must be built:** Move the wobble term from pitch to roll. Add the fixed 45° roll to the rest orientation. Both are one-line changes in the same function.
- **Numbers that matter:** shake **7 ticks = 0.35 s** ✅ already correct; shake curve `−sin(t_ticks × 3°) × t_ticks` degrees on **roll**; rest roll **+45°** on the arrow's own axis; heading lerp factor **0.2/tick**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** The arrow is drawn as crossed quads with "any two perpendiculars" — a roll about the shaft on crossed quads is a **no-op unless the two quads are at 45°/135° rather than 0°/90°**, so check the quad construction before assuming the roll will be visible. If the quads are symmetric, the 45° rest roll is genuinely invisible and only the shake matters. **This needs an eye I do not have.**

#### G3.17 — Riding poses · S · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** `player.animation.json`'s riding clips. `riding.arms` puts **both arms at −36°**. `riding.legs` is `[−81 − this, ∓18 − this, −this]` ⇒ legs pitched **−81°** and yawed **±18°** — note this is **not** the 90° splay one would guess; the rider's thighs are nearly horizontal and only slightly spread. `riding.root.position.y = variable.riding_y_offset`, which is **−3.0 pixels** and applies **only to minecart, boat, chest boat and strider**, not to land mounts. Vindicators use −72° instead of −81°.

  Seat positions come from the *mount's* `minecraft:rideable` component: horse `[0, 1.1, −0.2]`; sheep adult wooly `[0, 0.975, 0]`, sheared `[0, 0.9, 0]`, baby `[0, 0.70, −0.3]`; boat has **two seats** with `"lock_rider_rotation": 90`, while every land mount uses 0 — that is what lets a boat passenger look around freely while a horse rider's body follows the horse. [https://github.com/Mojang/bedrock-samples/blob/main/resource_pack/animations/player.animation.json]
- **What we have:** Nothing — no riding poses, and riding itself belongs to fragment 08. (Read in the code.)
- **What must be built:** Once mounts exist: a `riding` flag on the rider, the two rotations above, and per-mount seat offsets read from a species field rather than hard-coded per mount.
- **Numbers that matter:** arms **−36° = −0.6283 rad**; legs **−81° = −1.4137 rad** pitch, **±18° = ±0.3142 rad** yaw; vehicle Y offset **−3 units = −0.1875 blocks** for boats/minecarts only; horse seat **(0, 1.1, −0.2)**; `lock_rider_rotation` **90° for boats, 0 for land mounts**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** Blocked on fragment 08 (transport) landing rideable entities. The rotation-lock difference between boats and land mounts is the part most likely to be missed and it is the part players notice.

#### G3.18 — Boat paddles and minecart tilt · S · P3

*Noted for the dependency only — this belongs to fragment 08 (transport).* The reference's numbers, so they are not re-derived: boat paddle `xRot = clampedLerp(−π/3, −0.2617994, (sin(−rowTime) + 1)/2)` ⇒ **−60° → −15°**; `yRot = clampedLerp(−π/4, π/4, ...)` ⇒ **−45° → +45°**; rest-pose Z roll **11.25°**. **Boats do not rock on calm water** — only on `hurtTime` or inside a bubble column. Minecart tilt is `f5 = atan(velocity.y) × 73.0` degrees applied as `ZP(−f5)`, sampling the rail **0.3 blocks ahead and behind**, plus a **±0.002** per-entity-ID jitter so a train of carts does not move in lockstep. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Boat] [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecart]

### 3.4 Errors and inconsistencies noticed while reading

*Fragment 12 (`12-animation-errors.md`) already documents twelve defects inside the creature rig — F18.1 (Princepin left-arm/weapon), F18.2 (witch wind-up inverted), F18.3 (witch potion origin), F18.4 (`creature.age` never seeded, so herds sway in lockstep), F18.5 (biped arms at full leg amplitude instead of 1/1.4), F18.6 (hand-rolled quads bypass `modelScale` on baby chickens), F18.7 (`mirror` applied in one rig only), F18.8 (archer arrow ignores idle sway), F18.9 (sheep rig unguarded fall-through), F18.10 (`legBox` pivot uses the height swell), F18.11 (`kBipedArmLength` hard-coded three times), F18.12 (iron golem missing body/head roll). **None of them is repeated here.** What follows is what I found outside that fragment's scope.*

**1. `Main.cpp:6877–6893` · the fire animation hitches once every 3.2 seconds · confidence: certain (arithmetic).**
`waterAnimationSeconds` is advanced on the frame delta and wrapped to `kWaterLoop = kWaterFrames × kWaterFrameSeconds = 32 × 0.1 = 3.2 s`. The **fire frame is then derived from that same wrapped accumulator** at `kFireFrameSeconds = 0.055`. Since `3.2 / 0.055 = 58.18…`, the fire's frame index at the moment of the wrap is 58 mod 32 = **26**, and it jumps straight back to **0**. A player watching a torch, a campfire or a burning creature sees the flame visibly skip a beat **every 3.2 seconds, forever**. Two independent animations must not share one wrapped clock; give each its own accumulator (which G3.4's array does structurally). Secondary: `kFireFrameSeconds` should be **0.05** (1 tick/frame), not 0.055 — the reference runs fire at exactly one frame per tick.

**2. `ItemEntity.cpp:247, 251` · dropped-item bob and spin phase are derived from the item's live position · confidence: certain (arithmetic).**
```
bob  = ... sin(timeSeconds * kBobSpeed + drop.position.x) ...
spin =     timeSeconds * kSpinSpeed + drop.position.z
```
The reference assigns `bobOffs` **once at spawn** and never touches it again. Ours recomputes phase from `position.x` / `position.z` **every frame**, so any drop that is moving — sliding off a slope, pushed by flowing water, being drawn toward the player on pickup, or simply falling — has its phase rewritten continuously. The visible result is that a moving item's **spin rate jitters and can momentarily reverse**, and its bob stutters. This is the same rule fragment 12's F18.4 identifies as not having travelled: the squid rig seeds `jetPhase` correctly and nothing else does. One `float bobPhase` on the drop, set at spawn, fixes both.

**3. `ItemEntity.cpp:247` · an item stops bobbing whenever it is not on the ground · confidence: certain.**
The bob is gated on `drop.onGround`. There is a buoyancy path (`kFloatSpeed = 0.6f`), so an item floating in water — a very common sight, every time something is dropped into a river — sits **perfectly still**. So does one falling. The reference bobs unconditionally. Delete the gate.

**4. `Creature.cpp:57` · the damage flash is 30% too short, and the constant is doing two jobs · confidence: certain on the value, likely on the consequence.**
`kHurtSeconds = 0.35f` = 7 ticks against the reference's **10 ticks = 0.5 s**. But `hurtTimer` is also the knockback-override window at `Creature.cpp:4130` — while `health > 0 && hurtTimer > 0`, the creature's `wish` vector is discarded in favour of the shove velocity. So the "obvious" one-character fix silently lengthens every knockback by 43% and changes combat spacing. **Two timers, not one.** This is `CLAUDE.md`'s opening-box shape #3 in a slightly different dress — a number ported into a field that turned out to be measured against something else.

**5. `Creature.cpp:319` · mobs stop tracking you 23° early · confidence: certain on the number, worth checking by eye for consequences.**
`kMaxHeadTurn = 0.9f` rad = **51.6°**; the reference is **75°**. Circle a cow and its head detaches from you noticeably sooner than it should, then snaps back when you cross behind it. The neighbouring `kMaxHeadPitch = 0.7f` rad = 40.1° **is** right (reference 40°), which suggests 0.9 was a guess made next to a correct value — the classic "a rule that did not travel". Worth checking whether 75° exposes a neck seam on the wider models before committing.

**6. `Creature.cpp:74–80, 5297–5312` · one death rule for all 57 species, with the wrong easing · confidence: certain.**
Two separate things. (a) The easing is smoothstep `t²(3 − 2t)`, which is symmetric and slow at both ends; the reference is `min(sqrt(t × 1.6), 1)`, which is **front-loaded** — the body drops fast then settles. The durations are exactly right (12.5 ticks to 90°, 20 ticks total), so only the curve is wrong, and the difference is that ours looks like a controlled lie-down rather than a collapse. (b) The reference gives **spiders, cave spiders, silverfish and endermites an upside-down flip** and **squid no death animation at all**; ours rolls all 57 onto their side identically. A dying spider folding sideways like a cow is the most visible instance.

**7. `Projectile.cpp:366–369` · the arrow's post-impact shake bends its flight direction · confidence: certain on the axis, worth checking whether it is visible.**
`wobble = −sin(shake × 10) × shake × 0.6` is added to **pitch**. Pitch is the arrow's heading, so an arrow that has just embedded itself in a wall or a creature **waves its whole body up and down as though still steering**. The reference applies the identical decaying wobble to **roll**, about the shaft, so the arrow quivers in place. The duration (`kShakeSeconds = 0.35f` = 7 ticks) already matches the reference exactly, which makes this a one-word fix. Caveat: the arrow is drawn as crossed quads with "any two perpendiculars", so if those quads are axis-symmetric a roll may be invisible and the correct fix is to remove the pitch wobble and add the reference's fixed 45° rest roll to make the roll meaningful. **That needs an eye.**

**8. `Creature.cpp:348–359` · a grazing sheep never reaches the grass · confidence: certain.**
`kGrazeHeadPitch = 0.7f` rad = **40.1°** against the reference's **36°**, `kGrazeSeconds = 1.8f` against **2.0 s** — both small. The real gap is that the reference **translates the head down 9 units = 0.5625 blocks** over the first 4 ticks and holds it there, with a ±12.6° nibble at ~2.3 Hz, while ours only rotates. The head tips forward and hangs in the air above the grass for 1.8 seconds. All three missing pieces live inside the `beginHead`/`endHead` frame that already exists.

**9. `Creature.cpp:551–554` · every baby is a shrunken adult · confidence: certain.**
`kBabyScale = 0.55f` is uniform. The reference scales the **head** by 1.2–2.0 on top of a 0.4–0.5 body — a baby cow's head is **2.0×** with a `[0, 4, 4]` pivot offset — and for humanoids it swaps in an entirely separate `geometry.*.baby` model. The in-code comment ("one scale cannot do the middle") shows this was a known compromise rather than an oversight, but it is the most visible single wrong shape in the game and the fix is a field and three lines inside `beginHead`. Note the interaction with fragment 12's **F18.6**: baby chickens draw hand-rolled quads that bypass `modelScale` entirely, so they will not respond to this change until F18.6 is fixed.

**10. `Block.hpp:4388` / `ChunkMesher.cpp:927` · `lidTurns` is not a lid · confidence: certain, and it is a naming hazard rather than a bug.**
`lidTurns` is a **texture quarter-turn count** for blocks with asymmetric top textures (beds). It has nothing to do with chest lids. Anyone grepping for chest-lid animation — as this fragment's brief explicitly instructed — lands on it and concludes lids are implemented. They are not; `Chest.hpp` has no openness state at all. Worth a rename to `topTextureTurns` when the file is next touched.

**11. `Creature.cpp:2187` · the archer aim eases where the reference snaps · confidence: certain, and it is probably an improvement.**
`kAimRate = 6.0f` blends into the archer pose. Bedrock's archer animation controller has **no blend time on this transition** — the skeleton snaps to the aim pose. Recording it here so a future session comparing against the reference does not "fix" a deliberate improvement into a regression. If it ever needs to match exactly, the change is to set the rate very high, not to delete the easing.

**12. `Main.cpp:112` · `kSwingSeconds = 0.45f` is 50% longer than the reference's swing · confidence: certain on the number, unclear on the intent.**
The reference's hand swing is **6 ticks = 0.30 s**, and our creature attack swing at `Creature.cpp:266` is correctly `0.3f`. The player's is `0.45f`. Since nothing is drawn today it only governs attack rate and reach, so it may have been tuned for combat feel rather than animation — but **when G3.1 lands, these two must agree or the player's arm will visibly swing slower than a zombie's.** Decide deliberately at that point, and if 0.45 is kept, write down why.

**13. Interpolation audit — the project's own lesson is honoured everywhere I looked · confidence: certain.**
Checked specifically because the brief asked. There is **no fixed simulation tick loop** in this engine outside `Projectile.cpp`; everything runs on the variable per-frame `deltaSeconds`, with per-tick reference constants converted by `pow(k, dt/0.05f)` (`kLimbSwingLagPerTick`, `kStepSmoothPerTick`, `kFlapDecayPerTick`) and per-tick rates divided by 0.05 (`kFlapOpenRate`, `kFlapPhaseRate`, `kInsectWingPhaseRate`). The gait is **distance-driven**, which is the reference's own approach and is inherently interpolation-free. `Projectile.cpp` is the one subsystem with a fixed 0.05 s accumulator, and it **does** blend prev→current for both position (`:322`) and heading (`:361`). **No animation path steps where it should interpolate.** The one thing to watch: if a future block-entity framework (G3.2) introduces a second fixed-tick accumulator, it must either blend or — better — advance on `deltaSeconds` directly and avoid the problem entirely.

**14. Things I checked and found correct, so the time is not spent twice.**
The mob held-item transforms at `Creature.cpp:210–235` are **exactly** the reference's `item/handheld` and `item/generated` `thirdperson_righthand` entries (`{{0,−90,55},{0,4,0.5},0.85}` and `{{0,0,0},{0,3,1},0.55}`), with the left hand correctly derived by negating Y/Z rotation and the sideways translation — fragment 12 lists this as unaudited, and it is now audited and correct. `kAttackSwingSeconds = 0.3f` = 6 ticks matches. Both idle-sway frequencies (1.8 and 1.34 rad/s) and the amplitude (±0.05 rad about +0.05) are `animation.humanoid.bob` and the zombie arm oscillator to three significant figures. `kDeathTipSeconds` and `kDeathSeconds` are exactly 12.5 and 20 ticks. `kShakeSeconds` is exactly 7 ticks. `kWaterFrameSeconds = 0.1` is exactly `still_water_grey`'s 2 ticks/frame. Doors, trapdoors and fence gates snapping instantly **matches** the reference and is not a gap. The villager having no work or trade animation **matches Bedrock** and is not a gap. Falling blocks not rotating **matches**. Non-arrow projectiles being camera billboards with no spin **matches**. The 5-minute item despawn **matches**.

**Not verified — requires running the game, which I could not do.** Which side a creature currently tips onto in death. Whether a 75° head yaw exposes a neck seam. Whether the arrow's crossed quads make a roll visible. Whether the fire hitch in #1 is perceptible at a glance or only when stared at (the arithmetic is certain; the perceptibility is not). Whether the item-entity phase jitter in #2 reads as "wrong" or merely as "lively". Whether `kBabyScale = 0.55` plus a corrected head scale lands in the right place without also lowering the body scale to 0.5.

## 4. Creatures, behaviour and AI depth

**Scope:** Overworld-spawning mobs only — every Nether/End species (piglin, hoglin, blaze, ghast, strider, wither skeleton, magma cube, endermite, shulker, dragon, wither, zoglin) is permanently out and is **not** counted as a gap below, including the eight of them we already ship.

**Headline verdict:** What exists is a genuinely good *mob simulation* and almost no *mob game*. The species table and the priority-sorted behaviour table are the right architecture — they are a faithful, well-reasoned port of Bedrock's `minecraft:behavior.*` goal list, and adding a passive quadruped really is one row. But every mechanic that turns a mob into a system the player *uses* is absent: **there is no breeding, no taming, no riding and no trading**, four separate systems, none of which has a single line of code anywhere in `game/src`. Nineteen overworld species are missing, about nine of which are a table row plus a skin and ten of which need a new mechanic. The population layer is the weakest part: one flat cap of 44 creatures where Bedrock runs five independent caps, distance-only retirement where Bedrock has a 32 m/30 s random despawn plus a persistence flag, and a save record that drops a villager's bed, job and bell claim so a village permanently stops working after a reload.

**Completeness estimate:** roughly **45 %** of Bedrock's overworld mob behaviour by mechanic count, and closer to **25 %** weighted by what a player actually interacts with. Movement, aggression, targeting, fleeing, pathfinding, combat arbitration and the sensory model are 70–85 % there. Breeding/taming/riding/trading/raids are 0 %. Population management is ~30 %.

#### Roster: our 58 species against Bedrock's overworld list

Ours, overworld-relevant (**50**): Sheep, Cow, Pig, Bramble *(creeper)*, Chicken, Cat, Camel, Horse, Mule, Llama, Donkey, Goat, Rabbit, Wolf, Frog, Fox, Ocelot, Polar Bear, Panda, Slime ×3, Spider, Cave Spider, Zombie, Skeleton, Villager, Husk, Silverfish, Stray, Bogged, Zombie Villager, Witch, Wandering Trader, Drowned, Cod, Salmon, Pufferfish, Squid, Glow Squid, Turtle, Dolphin, Axolotl, Tropical Fish, Mooshroom, Skeleton Horse, Zombie Horse, Trader Llama, Bee, Iron Golem.

Ours, **out of scope** and not counted (8): Princepin, Princepin Brute, Zombie Princepin, Blackbone *(wither skeleton)*, Voidmite *(endermite)*, Magma Cube ×3. *(As flagged in the brief — yes, we already have magma cubes. Noted; moving on.)*

### 4.3 Gap detail

#### G4.1 — Breeding and baby growth · M · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** One food item per parent puts each into **love mode**. Both pathfind toward each other up to **8 blocks**, walk into each other for about **2.5 s**, drop **1–7 XP** (llama 1–8) and produce a baby. Parents then hold a **breeding cooldown of 5 minutes (6000 ticks)** — except **wolf and axolotl at 1 minute** and **turtle at 90 s**. Love mode expires after **30 s (600 ticks)** with no partner, and the animal is immediately re-feedable. Any two adults may breed, **including parent × child**. Babies take **20 minutes (24000 ticks)** to grow, snifflets 40 min. In **Bedrock**, feeding a baby removes **10 % of the *total* growth time, maximum 10 feedings** — this is a real BE/JE split, Java removes 10 % of the *remaining* time. Camel is a flat **10 s per cactus** in both. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Breeding](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Breeding), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Baby](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Baby)
  - **Foods (Bedrock):** wheat — cow, mooshroom, sheep, goat. carrot/potato/beetroot — pig. wheat/pumpkin/melon/beetroot/torchflower seeds, pitcher pod — chicken. any raw or cooked meat + rotten flesh — **tamed** wolf (BE excludes fish and rabbit stew from breeding; they heal only). raw cod/salmon — **tamed** cat, ocelot. golden apple / enchanted golden apple / golden carrot — **tamed** horse, donkey. hay bale — **tamed** llama, trader llama. dandelion/carrot/golden carrot — rabbit. seagrass — turtle (lays eggs on sand, at its spawn beach). bamboo — panda (**BE: ≥8 bamboo plants within radius 5 of *each* panda**, otherwise it just eats the bamboo). sweet berries / glow berries — fox (the kit trusts the breeder). any flower or flowering block — bee. slimeball — frog (lays frogspawn on water, hatches to tadpoles in 10 min). cactus — camel. torchflower seeds — sniffer (lays an egg item that must be placed). spider eye — armadillo. bucket of tropical fish — axolotl (returns a water bucket).
  - **Special cases:** horse × donkey → **mule** (infertile). Horse/donkey/llama must be **tamed** first. Sheep also grow faster by eating grass. Chickens are the only animal that both breeds directly and lays eggs unprompted.
- **What we have:** nothing. `babyChance` at spawn (`Creature.cpp:5017`, per-species rates in the table) and `Creature::scale` multiplying model *and* collision box. `scale` is written once and never touched again, so a lamb is a lamb permanently. `RESEARCH.md` §5.3 already carries the full number set and is marked **`ACTIVE — not built`**; that section can be marked used the day this lands.
- **What must be built:**
  1. Three fields on `Creature`: `loveTimer` (float, seconds), `breedCooldown` (float), `growTimer` (float, seconds remaining to adult; 0 = adult).
  2. Two fields on `CreatureSpecies`: `breedItems` (a small `ItemId` list or a predicate function, mirroring `professionForJobSite`'s "ask a family, never list ids" rule) and `breedCooldownSeconds` (default 300, wolf/axolotl 60, turtle 90).
  3. A **`Tempt`** behaviour row at priority 4 — Bedrock has it — so a held breeding item leads a herd. Tempt ranges: sheep/cow/pig 6 blocks, chicken a 6×4×6 box, rabbit 8 (approaches slowly), goat 10, frog 6, stray cat 10, wolf 8; break-off at **≥16 blocks in Bedrock** (≥10 in Java).
  4. A **`Breed`** row at priority 3 (Bedrock's own number — see `sheep.json`) that pathfinds to the nearest same-kind creature with `loveTimer > 0` within 8 m and, on 2.5 s of contact, emits a child and sets both cooldowns.
  5. A **`FollowParent`** row at priority 5 (baby: 6) so a herd reads as a family — Bedrock: babies follow *any* adult of the same species within 8 blocks.
  6. Growth: tick `growTimer` down, lerp `scale` from `kBabyScale` (0.55) to 1.0. **The collision box moves with it**, which the existing `bodyBox(species, feet, scale)` (`Creature.cpp:1225`) already handles.
  7. `growTimer`, `loveTimer` and `breedCooldown` all go into `SavedCreature` — see G4.2.
  8. Turtle eggs, frogspawn and sniffer eggs are **blocks/items**, not babies; treat them as a second phase, not a blocker.
- **Numbers that matter:** love 600 t / 30 s · partner search 8 blocks · kiss 50 t / 2.5 s · cooldown 6000 t / 300 s (wolf, axolotl 1200 t / 60 s; turtle 1800 t / 90 s) · growth 24000 t / 1200 s (snifflet 48000 t / 2400 s) · BE feed accelerator −10 % of total, cap 10 feeds · camel −200 t / −10 s flat · XP 1–7 (llama 1–8) · baby scale 0.55 (ours), Bedrock babies also walk faster and are pitched +6 semitones.
- **Risks / dependencies:** XP orbs do not exist, so the reward is silently dropped — acceptable, or land XP first. Watch the population cap: a working breeding pen will hit `kCreatureCeiling = 44` immediately and the retirement pass will start deleting animals the player built. **G4.3 and G4.11 (persistence) are effectively prerequisites for breeding to feel safe**, exactly as Bedrock makes bred animals persistent.

#### G4.2 — Population save/load completeness · S · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** a mob's POI claims (bed, job site, meeting point) are part of its saved data; a reloaded village resumes work immediately. `audit.md` §13.3 already reports this and it is **confirmed by reading**.
- **What we have:** `SavedCreature` (`WorldStore.hpp:76–101`) carries kind, x, y, z, yaw, health, scale, `charged`, `playerBuilt`, `profession` and nothing else. `Creatures::restore` (`Creature.cpp:4539–4557`) sets `profession` and leaves `bedCell`/`jobCell`/`meetCell` at their `{0,-1,0}` default. `alreadyClaimed` (`Creature.cpp:~2857`) scans other creatures' `jobCell`, which is now `-1` for everybody, so **the workstation reads as free and a second villager takes it**. `Creature::variant` is likewise unsaved — the header says so itself (`Creature.hpp:1132`: *"Not saved yet — a reloaded fish comes back in a different livery"*).
- **What must be built:** bump the save format version; add `bedCell`, `jobCell`, `meetCell` (three `ivec3`), `variant` (u8), and — once G4.1 lands — `loveTimer`, `breedCooldown`, `growTimer`, plus a `persistent` bit for G4.11. Re-validate claims on load: if the claimed block is gone or is no longer a job site, clear the claim rather than trusting the file (the same repair `professionForJobSite` implies).
- **Numbers that matter:** three `ivec3` = 36 bytes per villager; a 14-resident village costs ~500 bytes. Nothing here is a size problem.
- **Risks / dependencies:** touching the save format needs the version bump `kChunkFormatVersion`-style discipline; there is **no autosave at all** (`audit.md` §"Saves that survive a restart"), so any test of this has to be a clean quit.

#### G4.3 — Mob cap categories, spawn cycle and despawning · M · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** three independent limiters. (1) A **global cap of 200** ticked mobs, environmental spawns only — breeding, spawn eggs and spawners bypass it. (2) **Population-control caps per 9×9-chunk region (144 × 144 blocks)** centred on the candidate chunk — *not* per-player as Java 1.18+ does. Overworld: Ambient surface 0 / cave 2 · Animal surface 4 / cave 0 · **Monster surface 8 / cave 16** · Pillager 8/8 · Water Animal surface 36 / cave 0. Cat has its own category. Surface-vs-cave is decided by **how the mob spawned**, not where it now is; converted mobs and structure spawns are always "cave", spawner mobs always "surface". (3) **Per-mob density caps** — creeper 5, phantom 5, dolphin 5, drowned 5 ocean / 2 river, cod 20, salmon 10/4, squid 4/2, pufferfish 3, tropical fish 20+20. Spawn attempts run at **11/2000 per chunk per tick** (0.55 %/chunk/tick, ~9.1 s mean per chunk). Spawn shell **24–44 blocks** at simulation distance 4, **24–128 blocks** at 6+, with a coding restriction near ~96 blocks horizontally (MCPE-102197). Cluster spawning does a downward column search picking **surface first, then every cave layer to bedrock**. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_spawning](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_spawning)
  - **Despawn:** instant if >128 blocks from the nearest player or in an edge-of-simulation chunk (sim ≥6); >44 blocks at sim 4; **fish always at >40 blocks**; **random 1-in-800 per tick when >32 blocks away and not damaged for 30 s (600 ticks)** — half-life ≈ 555 ticks / 27.75 s; everything, persistent or not, despawns at **Y ≤ −128**.
  - **Light:** animals need **combined light ≥ 7**; hostiles need **sky light ≤ 7 AND block light = 0**. Bat 0–4, mooshroom 9–15 (the only mob at 9), slime-chunk slimes ignore light entirely.
- **What we have:** one cap. `capacityFor(radius)` (`Creature.cpp:578`) scales `kMaxCreatures = 14` by area against `kBaseRadius = 90` and clamps to `kCreatureCeiling = 44`. At a 12-chunk render distance the active radius is 384 m, so **44 creatures of all kinds share a 384 m sphere** where Bedrock allows 66 in a 144 m square plus a 200 global. The continuous cycle fires every 2.5 s (`kSpawnInterval`), makes at most 8 attempts and adds **at most one creature**, in a shell 0.27R–0.85R (`:38–39`). The chunk-generation pass covers 10 % of chunks (`kChunkSpawnChance = 0.10`, `:571`) with a doubled ceiling (`generatedCeiling`, `:587`). Per-species `maxLoaded` (`Creature.hpp:~590`) *is* Bedrock's density cap and is correct. Despawn is distance-only (`Creature.cpp:4834–4842`). `RESEARCH.md` §4 already flags "one cap for every category" as the known gap.
- **What must be built:**
  1. A `SpawnCategory` field on `CreatureSpecies` (Ambient / Animal / Cat / Monster / Pillager / WaterAnimal), and `capacityFor` replaced by a per-category table. Adopt Bedrock's *ratios* rather than its absolute numbers — our active radius and our world height differ — but keep monsters ≫ animals ≫ ambient.
  2. A surface/cave bit on `Creature`, set at spawn from whether the spot was the highest spawnable block. That one bit is what makes a cave system feel dangerous while the surface stays walkable.
  3. Random despawn: `1/800` per tick beyond 32 m with a 600-tick damage-free requirement, gated on a `persistent` flag (G4.11).
  4. The column search: currently one candidate Y per attempt (`surface + 1`, or `waterColumnY`). Bedrock searches downward and attempts a herd at *every* qualifying layer — this is what actually populates caves.
- **Numbers that matter:** all of the above. Ours today: 14/44 cap, 2.5 s interval, 8 attempts, 1 spawn, 0.27R–0.85R shell, 10 % chunk chance.
- **Risks / dependencies:** raising the cap is a frame-rate decision — `audit.md` notes `separate()` is O(N²) (`Creature.cpp:4412`) and every creature's mesh is rebuilt and re-uploaded per frame (`Main.cpp:6430`). **Measure before raising the cap**, per the project's own rule; the mesh upload is the likelier wall, not the AI.

#### G4.4 — Taming and pets · M · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** wolf — **bones, 1/3 chance per bone**; tamed wolf goes from **8 HP to 40 HP**, gains a dyeable collar, sits/stands on use, follows the owner, teleports to the owner when far, attacks whatever the owner attacks and whatever attacks the owner (**except creepers and other same-owner wolves**), and is healed by meat. Cat — **raw cod or raw salmon, 1/3**; tamed cat goes **10 HP → 20 HP** (a Bedrock-specific value; Java keeps 10), sits, follows, gifts items in the morning, and **scares creepers and phantoms**. Parrot — **seeds, 1/10** (not 1/3); rides the shoulder, mimics mob sounds, dances to a jukebox. Ocelot and fox — **trust, not taming**: an ocelot trusts on a 1/3 raw-fish feed and stops fleeing; a fox kit born from two bred foxes trusts the breeder. Horse/donkey/mule/llama/trader llama — **repeated mounting** until the buck stops, governed by a hidden **temper** (horse 0–100, llama and trader llama 0–30) that food raises. **Taming grants persistence.** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Taming](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Taming)
- **What we have:** nothing. `retaliates = false` on cat/fox/ocelot (`Creature.cpp:680, 743, 751`) is exactly Bedrock's "no `hurt_by_target` goal", which is the right foundation. `playerBuilt` on the iron golem (`Creature.hpp:~1170`) is already a per-individual, saved, temperament-changing flag — **that is the pattern to copy**, not to reinvent.
- **What must be built:** `ownerId` (or a plain `tamed` bit, since single-player has one owner — a deliberate simplification the no-multiplayer decision earns us), `sitting`, `collarColour`, `temper` on `Creature`; a `tameItem`/`tameChance` pair on `CreatureSpecies`; behaviour rows for **`FollowOwner`** (priority ~5, teleport when >12 blocks and a safe landing exists), **`Sit`** (priority ~2, claims Move), **`OwnerHurtTarget`** and **`OwnerHurtByTarget`** (priority 1, targeting, claim nothing — they fit the existing producer/consumer split exactly). Taming implies persistence, so G4.11 rides along.
- **Numbers that matter:** wolf bone 1/3 · cat/ocelot fish 1/3 · parrot seed 1/10 · wolf HP 8 → 40 · cat HP 10 → 20 (BE) · owner-teleport threshold ~12 blocks · horse temper 0–100, llama 0–30 · BE wolf has **9 variants** with biome-specific spawn rules (pale, ashen, black, chestnut, rusty, snowy, spotted, striped, woods) and armadillo-scute wolf armour.
- **Risks / dependencies:** a tamed wolf that helps you fight needs the creature-on-creature hit path (`m_hits`/`applyHits`, `Creature.cpp:4382`) rather than `strike` — see 4.4 item 2, which is the *same* bug from the other end.

#### G4.5 — Villager trading and experience · L · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** five career levels — **Novice 0, Apprentice 10, Journeyman 70, Expert 150, Master 250** villager XP. **Bedrock unlocks up to three trade slots per level and a villager ends with 7–10 slots**, each slot rolling one trade from its own pool (Java instead offers up to two new trades per level from a shared pool). Trading pays the player **3–6 XP, plus 5 more if the villager levels**, and gives the villager **10 s of Regeneration I** with pink particles. Restocking happens **twice per work day** and requires the villager to reach its workstation. Prices carry **demand**, a per-trade counter that raises the price of things bought often. **Hero of the Village in Bedrock is level I only — a flat 30 % discount** at every villager in the world (Java scales I–V to 55 %). A villager whose job-site block is removed **before its first trade** reverts to unemployed; after the first trade the profession and the offers lock forever. Zombification on death by zombie: **Easy 0 %, Normal 50 %, Hard 100 %**. Curing takes **3600–6000 ticks (3–5 min)** with weakness + a golden apple; nearby iron bars/beds give only ≈4.2 % average speed-up. **Bedrock iron-golem spawning is population-based, not panic-based**: ≥20 beds, ≥10 villagers, 75 % of villagers worked in the last Minecraft day, 100 % bed-linked, then 1/700 per tick. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trading](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trading), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Villager](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Villager)
- **What we have:** the *approach* half and none of the *economy* half. `ClaimPoi` gives every villager a profession by claiming a block (`Creature.cpp:3078`), `Work`/`Mingle`/`Sleep` run the daily schedule, 14 outfits are composited on the skin sheet (`Creature.hpp:36–45`). **The brief's "14 trades" are 14 outfits.** There is no trade table, no price, no emerald sink, no trading screen (`game/src/hud/` holds six widgets, none of them a container UI beyond `InventoryScreen`), and **no XP anywhere**.
- **What must be built:** (a) an XP orb entity and a player XP total — a prerequisite shared with G4.1; (b) a trade table, one row per (profession, tier, slot) with item in / item out / price range / max uses / demand; (c) a trading screen, which is the *second* container UI and therefore the point at which `InventoryScreen`'s layout code should be generalised; (d) `villagerXp`, `tier`, `tradeUses[]` and a `firstTradeDone` lock on `Creature`, all saved; (e) restock on the existing `workTimer`, which already models Bedrock's 12.5 s at the block plus 10 s cooldown.
- **Numbers that matter:** tier thresholds 0/10/70/150/250 · BE 7–10 slots, ≤3 unlocked per level · player XP 3–6 per trade, +5 on level-up · villager Regeneration I for 200 ticks / 10 s · restock ×2 per work day · HotV **level I, 30 %, 48000 ticks / 40 min** · curing 3600–6000 t · zombification 0/50/100 % by difficulty (we run Normal only) · BE golem quota 20 beds / 10 villagers / 75 % worked / 1-in-700 per tick.
- **Risks / dependencies:** this is the single biggest content-authoring job in the whole roster area — thirteen professions × five tiers. It is also the gate on G4.9 (Hero of the Village is a trade discount). Our villages cap at **14 residents** (`Village.hpp` `kMaxResidents`) and one golem, so the Bedrock golem quota can never trigger — the code comment in `Village.hpp` already says so, and that is a correct, documented divergence.

#### G4.6 — Riding and mounts · L · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** horses roll **health 15–30**, **speed 0.1125–0.3375** (≈4.8–14.5 blocks/s) and **jump strength 0.4–1.0** (≈1.25–5.3 blocks); breeding averages the parents' stats with a third random draw. Donkeys and mules take a chest (**15 slots**). Llamas take carpet decoration, have a **strength** stat setting inventory size, form **caravans** on leads, and **spit for 1 HP (1.5 Hard)**. A pig with a saddle is steered by a carrot on a stick with a boost. Camels carry **two riders**, dash, sit, and are tall enough that most hostiles cannot reach the rider. Equines take **half fall damage beyond 6 blocks**. Skeleton horses in Bedrock need no saddle to be controlled. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Horse](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Horse), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Riding](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Riding)
- **What we have:** `ItemId::Saddle` (`Item.hpp:330`, `:993`) and five equine species with `stepHeight = 1.0` and `jumpHeight = 0` (`Creature.cpp:692–711`) — long-legged so they glide up ledges, which is Bedrock's own arrangement and already right. Nothing rides anything.
- **What must be built:** a passenger relationship (`riderId` on the creature, or a `mountId` on the player); movement control transfer, which is a `Player.cpp` change rather than a creature one; a charged-jump input; per-individual `maxHealth`/`speed`/`jumpStrength` rolled at spawn and **saved** (today `CreatureSpecies::health` is a species constant, so all horses are identical); the horse inventory screen (shares G4.5's container work).
- **Numbers that matter:** HP 15–30 · speed attribute 0.1125–0.3375 → convert at the same ×17–19 band the rest of our roster uses, not the raw number (**the wrong-unit trap this project has already paid for**) · jump 0.4–1.0 → 1.25–5.3 blocks · chest 15 slots · llama spit 1 / 1 / 1.5 · equine fall: 6 free blocks then half damage.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the first thing in the game where the player's own physics is subordinated to another entity's. Do it *after* the camera and input work in §2, not before.

#### G4.7 — The nine cheap missing species · M · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour (spawn data straight from `Mojang/bedrock-samples:behavior_pack/spawn_rules/`):** bat — Ambient, weight 10, **herd 8–8**, brightness **0–4**, on stone/granite/diorite/andesite/tuff/deepslate, underground only, 6 HP. Parrot — weight 40, herd 1–2, light 7–15, jungle grass, 6 HP, 5 variants. Armadillo — weight 10 savanna / 6 mesa, herd 2–3, light 7–15, 12 HP, rolls up when a player sprints or rides nearby or when undead approach, drops scutes. Sniffer — **no spawn rules at all** (egg only), 14 HP, always persistent. Tadpole — no spawn rules (frogspawn only), 6 HP. Snow golem — built, always persistent, 4 HP. Pillager — **no environmental spawn conditions**: outposts, patrols and raids only; 24 HP, crossbow 2–3/3–5/5–7. Vindicator — 24 HP, iron axe, **BE unarmed 5/8/12**, mansion and raids, always persistent. Evoker — 24 HP, fangs **6 flat in Bedrock** (Java 4/6/9), summons vexes, always persistent.
- **What we have:** the archetypes all exist. `flies` (bee) covers bat and parrot; the quadruped rig covers armadillo and sniffer; `swims` covers the tadpole; the villager/witch biped rig covers pillager, vindicator, evoker and snow golem; `shootsArrows` + `heldMainHand` covers the pillager's crossbow with no new machinery.
- **What must be built:** nine rows in `kSpecies`, nine skin allocations on the 128-wide sheet (`kCreatureSheetHeight` must grow and `Main.cpp` checks the PNG against it), nine `spawnsIn` cases, nine `creatureTags` entries, nine loot rules, nine spawn eggs (the egg run is arithmetic off the enum, so it is free). **Bat needs the Ambient cap from G4.3 or it will compete with animals.** Armadillo needs a roll-up state (one bool + a model swap, the pufferfish's `puffs` pattern exactly).
- **Numbers that matter:** as above. Note the sheet: `kCreatureSheetWidth = 128`, `kCreatureSheetHeight = 4704` today (`Creature.hpp:27–28`) — every net origin is measured against these two.
- **Risks / dependencies:** **grep every new enumerator's name before writing it** — this project has added the same id twice, twice. And per `ASSETS-REFERENCE.md`, adding anything visible means one row in `tools/make-reference-blocks.ps1`/`make-creature-skins.ps1` plus a flat-colour placeholder under `assets/`, never hand-drawn art.

#### G4.8 — Mob-specific quirks batch · L · P1

Grouped because each is small and none is worth a milestone alone. All Bedrock unless marked.

| Quirk | Bedrock rule | Ours |
|---|---|---|
| Sheep shearing + wool colour | Shears give **1–3 wool**; the sheep regrows it by **`behavior.eat_block`** (success chance **0.001/tick adult, 0.02/tick baby**, `time_until_eat` **1.8 s**); colour weights white 81836 / grey, light grey, brown 5000 each / black 3000 / **pink 164**; breeding mixes parent colours as dyes | `grazes` and the 1.8 s `eatTimer` already exist (`Creature.hpp:~430`, `EatBlock` row at priority 5) and eat grass — but **nothing tracks a fleece**, sheep are always white, and `ToolKind::Shears` is a block tool only (the shears rows live at `Mining.hpp:181`) |
| Chicken egg laying | One egg every **6000–12000 ticks (5–10 min)** | Absent. The *hatch* half exists (`Main.cpp:6085`) at the correct 1/8 and 1/4-of-those-gives-4 odds |
| Mooshroom | Bowl → **mushroom stew**; shears → drops 5 mushrooms and **becomes a cow**; brown variant from lightning; brown + flower → suspicious stew | Milking works; the rest is absent |
| Goat | Rams stationary mobs at random; ramming a solid block **drops a goat horn**; screaming variant; **jumps 10 blocks** | Absent; the goat is a plain quadruped |
| Fox | Carries one item in its mouth, picks up items, **eats sweet berries**, sleeps by day, snow variant, drops what it carries | `hunts = Fowl \| Critter \| Fish` and `retaliates = false` are right; item-carrying absent |
| Panda | Seven personalities from two genes (main + hidden), **weak variant 10 HP** vs 20, lazy speed 0.07, aggressive damage 4/6/9, worried pandas hide in thunderstorms | One flat row, **and it has no attack at all** (see 4.4) |
| Bee | Nests/hives, pollination, honey level 0–5, **stings once and dies**, angered by harvesting without a campfire, 1–1 herd | The flier archetype and 25 s anger exist; no hive, no flower, no pollen, no death-on-sting |
| Turtle | Lays **1–4 eggs** on its home beach, eggs hatch faster at night, **zombies stomp them deliberately**, baby drops a **scute** on maturing | Absent |
| Dolphin | **Dolphin's Grace** boost to a swimming player, leads to shipwreck/ruin treasure when fed raw cod, drowns if kept out of water, hostile to guardians | `dryOutSeconds` exists; the rest absent |
| Axolotl | **Plays dead** below 50 % HP and regenerates, bucket capture, hunts fish/squid/drowned/guardians, five variants (blue at 1/1200) | Five variants exist; behaviour absent |
| Armadillo → wolf armour | Scutes are brushed or dropped; armour equips onto a tamed wolf | Both mobs absent |
| Cat | Gifts an item each morning after sleeping on/near the owner's bed; **creepers and phantoms flee cats** | `Bramble.avoids = Feline` at 6 m already exists (`Creature.cpp:673`) — the cat half is done; the phantom does not exist |
| Sniffer | Sniffs, digs **torchflower/pitcher pod** seeds from suitable ground | Absent |
| Frog | Eats **small slimes** with its tongue, three variants by biome; froglights are Nether-adjacent (**noted, skipped**) | Absent |

#### G4.9 — Illagers, raids, pillager outposts · XL · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** since **BE 1.21.0**, killing a raid captain no longer grants Bad Omen — it drops an **Ominous Bottle**, which when drunk gives **Bad Omen I–V for 1:40:00 (120000 ticks)**. Entering a village's **64 × 23 × 64 trigger box** converts it to **Raid Omen I for 600 ticks / 30 s**, and the raid begins when that expires. **In Bedrock the Bad Omen level has no effect on the raid at all** — no bonus waves, no enchant scaling, no Hero-of-the-Village scaling; the level only matters to trial spawners. Waves: **Easy 3, Normal 5, Hard 7, and Bedrock has no bonus waves.** Exact Bedrock composition — W1: 4 pillagers. W2: 3 pillagers + 2 vindicators. W3: 3 pillagers + 1 ravager. W4: 3 pillagers + 3 witches. W5: 4 vindicators + 1 ravager + 1 evoker + 1 ravager-with-pillager-rider. W6: 5 pillagers + 2 vindicators + 1 evoker. W7: 6 vindicators + 1 witch + 2 evokers + 1 ravager-with-pillager-rider + 1 ravager-with-evoker-rider. Totals **13 / 26 / 45 mobs**. Raiders spawn **all at once at one valid location** inside a **128 × 32 × 128 region**, above or below ground, **light and player proximity irrelevant**, on any block except leaves and scaffolding; a failed spawn attempt **ends that wave immediately**. Inter-wave cooldown **300 ticks / 15 s**; the raid expires after **48000 ticks / 40 min**; raiders **never despawn and do not count toward the mob cap** during a raid. Bedrock's boss bar shows the **count** of remaining raiders, not their health, and **Bedrock raid waves contain no captains**. Victory gives **Hero of the Village I for 48000 ticks / 40 min** to every player who killed at least one raider. Extra loot roll on raider death: **65 % Easy/Normal, 80 % Hard**. Outposts generate **8 pillagers including the captain**, respawn them continually, and hold cages with an **iron golem (85 %)** and an **allay (50 %)**. Patrols: herd **2–5** with one captain, `world_age_filter` ≥ 6000 ticks, `delay_filter` 600–660 s, `spawn_chance` 20, distance 24–48, suppressed within 48 blocks of a village. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Raid](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Raid), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Pillager_Outpost](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Pillager_Outpost), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bad_Omen](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bad_Omen)
- **What we have:** nothing at all — zero occurrences of pillager, vindicator, evoker, ravager, vex, raid, outpost or Bad Omen. Villages exist (`Village.cpp`, 1342 lines) with a bell (`meetCell`), residents and one golem.
- **What must be built, in order:** (1) the illager species rows from G4.7; (2) a status-effect carrier on the player (Bad Omen / Raid Omen / Hero of the Village) — `Effects.hpp` already exists (351 lines) and should be checked first; (3) an outpost structure in `Structures.cpp` with its own respawn pass; (4) a raid state machine owned by whatever owns villages, with a wave table, a spawn-location search and a boss bar in `hud/`; (5) evoker fangs and vex summoning, both new attack shapes; (6) the ravager's charge.
- **Risks / dependencies:** genuinely XL, and it wants G4.5 (HotV is a discount on trades that do not exist yet) and G4.3 (raiders must be exempted from the cap and from despawning). **Split it**: illagers as ordinary hostiles first, then outposts, then raids.

#### G4.10 — Phantom and insomnia · S · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** spawns when a player has not slept or died for **3 in-game days (72000 ticks / 1 h real)**, above Y 64 with sky access, in groups of 1–4, **surface density cap 5**, weight 100, brightness 0–7. **20 HP; Bedrock damage 4 / 6 / 9** — much higher than Java's 2/2/3. Swoops from above, burns in daylight, is **repelled by cats**, drops **0–1 phantom membrane**.
- **What we have:** the `flies` archetype (bee), `burnsInDay`, and cat-avoidance already expressed as a tag mask. No insomnia timer on the player.
- **What must be built:** an "ticks since sleep or death" counter on the player (saved with `player.dat`), one species row, and a swoop behaviour — a dive at the target with a pull-up, which is a new movement pattern but a small one.
- **Numbers that matter:** 72000 ticks · Y > 64 with sky access · groups 1–4 · density 5 · 20 HP · **4/6/9 damage [BE]** · membrane 0–1.

#### G4.11 — Leads, name tags and a persistence flag · S · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** a mob becomes permanent when it is ridden, **named with a name tag**, **tempted with food**, **bred or born from breeding**, **tamed**, spawned by egg or command, cured from a zombie villager, or **leashed — and it stays persistent after being unleashed**. Picking up an item also does it (dispenser-equipped armour does not). Always-persistent overworld mobs: allay, iron golem, snow golem, villager, sniffer, evoker, vindicator, elder guardian. **Attacking a mob does not make it persistent.** Wandering traders and their llamas despawn after 40–60 minutes (the wiki flags this claim `{{verify}}` — treat as low confidence).
- **What we have:** nothing; every creature is retired purely on distance.
- **What must be built:** a `persistent` bit on `Creature`, saved; set it from taming, breeding, naming and leashing; make the retirement pass respect it — but keep the `y < -8` escape hatch, because Bedrock despawns even persistent mobs at Y ≤ −128. A lead is a second entity relationship (a rope constraint) and can wait; the **flag** is the load-bearing half and is nearly free.

#### G4.12 — Mob-vs-mob hostility widened · S · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour** ([https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_infighting](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_infighting), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_fleeing](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_fleeing)): the parts we are missing, expressed as tag edits rather than new code —
  - **Iron golem** hunts every monster **except creepers** — ours already does this exactly right via an absent `Monster` tag on the Bramble.
  - **Skeleton/stray/bogged** hunt **baby turtles and iron golems**; **spiders and cave spiders** hunt **iron golems**; **slimes, witches and (BE) silverfish** hunt iron and snow golems.
  - **Zombie/husk/zombie villager/drowned** hunt **villager, wandering trader, iron golem, baby turtle** and (BE) **snow golem**. Bedrock's `zombie.json` `nearest_attackable_target` uses `within_radius: 25`, `must_see: true`, `must_see_forget_duration: 17`, with per-filter `max_dist` 35 for all of them and **`must_see: false` for villager and wandering trader** — a zombie smells a villager through a wall.
  - **Drowned** hunt **axolotls**; **guardians** hunt axolotls, squid and glow squid; **axolotls** hunt every fish plus drowned and guardians.
  - **Wild wolf** hunts sheep, rabbit, fox, **baby turtle**, and the whole skeletal family — ours has `Grazer | Critter | Vulpine | Skeletal`, so only baby turtles are missing.
  - **Polar bear** hunts foxes (ours does) and is a **pack retaliator only when a cub is attacked**; **llamas** hunt wild wolves; **pufferfish** defensively attack the axolotl and all non-aquatic mobs.
  - **Fleeing:** creeper and **phantom** flee cats/ocelots; **rabbits in Bedrock flee every monster** except hoglins and the dragon; **worried pandas in Bedrock flee all non-panda mobs**; skeletons flee wolves (ours does, 6 m); **spiders flee armadillos**; villagers flee the full undead+illager list; **dolphins flee guardians**.
  - **A Bedrock quirk worth knowing before anyone "fixes" ours:** `minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type` in Bedrock ignores `max_dist`/`max_flee` and effectively uses a **3×3×3 box for every mob** (MCPE-182041). Our per-species `avoidRange` is *better than the reference* and should stay.
- **What must be built:** widen `CreatureTag` with `Golem` and `Hatchling` (or gate on `scale < 1`), then edit `hunts`/`avoids` masks on maybe fifteen rows. Almost all of this is table data.

#### G4.13 to G4.19 — briefly

- **G4.13 Mob equipment (M/P2):** Bedrock arms monsters by regional difficulty — armour and weapon chances, enchant levels 5 on Easy and 5–19 on Normal/Hard. Ours has a species-constant `heldMainHand` and a behaviour-driven `heldOverride`, which is the right split; what is missing is a per-individual equipment array and a pickup goal (`behavior.pickup_items`, `equip_item`). Blocked on the armour system (`Item.hpp` carries `armourDefence`/`armourToughness` for all 24 pieces and nothing reads them — see §3).
- **G4.14 Mob griefing (S/P2):** zombies break doors above a regional-difficulty threshold; zombies deliberately stomp turtle eggs (`behavior.stomp_turtle_egg`, priority 5 in `zombie.json`); endermen pick up and place a whitelist of blocks. All three need the same thing: a creature that may *request* a block change, handed back to the main thread exactly as `takeGrazed()` already does (`Creature.hpp:1277`). **The mechanism exists; only the callers are missing.**
- **G4.15 Structure spawning + spawners (M/P2):** Bedrock fires a structure spawn whenever a cluster attempt succeeds in a chunk holding a hard-coded spot — swamp hut → witch, monument → guardian, outpost → pillager — and lets structure spawns exceed the population cap **by 1**. Monster spawners: **16-block activation, 200–799 tick delay, 4 attempts per cycle, nearby-entity cap 6 of the same type**, Bedrock's cap volume **16 × 10 × 16** from the block's lower NW corner and a **4-block taxicab spread ±1 Y**. We have spawner blocks in the catalogue and no spawner behaviour.
- **G4.16 Guardians (L/P2):** guardian 30 HP, laser 4/6/9 + spikes 2/2/3, elder 80 HP, laser 5/8/12, Mining Fatigue III aura. Needs an ocean monument and a beam attack with a charge-up — the beam is the only genuinely new rendering work.
- **G4.17 Enderman (M/P2):** 40 HP, damage 4.5/7/10.5, **follow range 64** (the widest on the roster), teleports on damage and in daylight, is provoked by being looked at within a narrow cone, carries a block, takes damage from water. The stare check is a new sensory mode; the rest fits the existing model.
- **G4.18 Wild villager/trader spawning (XS/P2):** Bedrock has **no `spawn_rules` file for villager, wandering trader, trader llama, iron golem, snow golem, sniffer, tadpole, mule or vex** — they are never environmentally spawned. Ours spawns villagers on any grassland at weight 0.5 (`Creature.cpp:856`, `spawnsIn` at `:3348`), trader llamas in the highlands (`:1134`), and wandering traders anywhere (`:949`). Fix: set `weight = 0` for these, as the iron golem row already does (`:1214`), and give the wandering trader a timed village-adjacent spawn with two leashed trader llamas and a despawn timer.
- **G4.19 Warden / creaking / breeze (XL/P3):** all three are Overworld by dimension and all three are really *structure* features. Warden needs sculk, vibration sensing, darkness and a sonic boom (500 HP, 16/30/45 melee, 6/10/15 ranged, knockback resistance 1.0, despawns after 1200 ticks without a detection). Creaking needs a creaking heart block, a 16-horizontal/8-vertical spawn link, and an invulnerable-while-linked rule. Breeze needs trial chambers and wind charges. **Park all three.**

### 4.4 Errors and inconsistencies noticed while reading

1. **`Creature.cpp:4995` · the continuous spawner falls back to `Sheep` when the weighted roll misses · confidence: certain (code path).** `auto chosen = CreatureKind::Sheep;` with no `Count` guard, against `Creature.cpp:4651`/`:4659` in `populateChunks`, which does exactly the right thing with `CreatureKind::Count` and a `continue`. Already in `audit.md` §13.4 — **confirmed, and worse than reported**: the fallback then computes `spawnY` as `speciesInfo(chosen).swims ? swimY : y` (`:5008`), so a roll that missed in an ocean cell puts a **sheep on the seabed** with `canSpawnAt` never asked about it. Fix is the one line the other copy already has.
2. **`Creature.cpp` `Creatures::strike` (called from `Projectile.cpp:243`) · a mob's arrow that clips another creature is blamed on the player · confidence: certain.** `audit.md` §13.2 — **confirmed by reading**. `strike` is the player's melee path and sets `threatId = 0`, which means "the player did it" (`Creature.hpp:~1090`). A skeleton shooting past you into a villager, a wolf or an iron golem turns that animal — and via `alertNeighbours` (`Creature.cpp:4461`) its whole herd — hostile to you. The correct path (`m_hits`/`applyHits`, `:4382`) sits right beside it. **This gets worse the moment taming lands** (G4.4): your own dog will turn on you.
3. **`WorldStore.hpp:76–101` + `Creature.cpp:4539–4557` · villager bed/job/bell claims are not saved · confidence: certain.** `audit.md` §13.3 — **confirmed by reading the struct.** `SavedCreature` has no `bedCell`/`jobCell`/`meetCell`; `restore` leaves them at `{0,-1,0}`. `alreadyClaimed` then sees every workstation as free, so a second villager duplicates the trade. Villages look right after a reload and never function again.
4. **`Creature.hpp:~1128` · `Creature::variant` is not saved · confidence: certain (the comment says so).** A reloaded axolotl, tropical fish or wolf comes back in a different livery. Cosmetic, and it is waiting on the same save-format bump as item 3 — do both at once.
5. **`Creature.cpp:768` (Panda row) vs `:1694` (`hurtByTargetStart`) · the panda's anger fields are dead code · confidence: certain.** The row carries `.angerSeconds = 500.0f, .alertRange = 41.0f` — the polar bear's numbers — but **no `attackDamage`**, and `hurtByTargetStart` returns false when `attackDamage <= 0`. So a struck panda always falls through to `Panic` (`:1843`, which requires exactly that) and the two tuned fields never do anything. This is bug shape #14 — a row copied without the one field that made it right. Bedrock's panda deals **2/2/3, aggressive variant 4/6/9**, and only the aggressive personality retaliates properly; the fix is a damage value plus (eventually) the personality genes.
6. **`Creature.cpp:3348` (`spawnsIn`, Villager case) · stale comment and a real divergence · confidence: certain.** The comment reads *"Villages do not exist yet, so it simply lives on open grassland"* — villages have existed since M2x (`Village.cpp`, 1342 lines, and the villager row sets `keepsHouse = true`). The comment is stale **and** the behaviour it describes is a divergence: Bedrock ships **no villager spawn rules at all**. See G4.18.
7. **`Creature.cpp:836–844` (Skeleton row) · stale comment · confidence: certain.** *"No bow yet, so it closes and hits rather than shooting"* and *"until we have arrows a punching animation would tell the player it is something it is not"* — the very same row now sets `.shootsArrows = true, .heldMainHand = ItemId::Bow`. The code is right; the comment above it is three milestones out of date and would mislead the next reader.
8. **Species count · the roster is 58, not 57 · confidence: certain.** `CreatureKind` has 58 enumerators before `Count`, `kSpecies` has 58 rows, and `static_assert` at `Creature.cpp:1221` binds them. The "57 species" figure in `CLAUDE.md`, `audit.md` and the milestone notes predates the iron golem row (`:1212`). One-line doc fix in several places.
9. **`Creature.cpp:3064–3106` · there is no `move_to_water` / `move_to_land` behaviour row · confidence: certain that the row is absent (0 matches for `moveToWater`/`moveToLand` anywhere in `Creature.cpp`); worth checking whether it bites.** Bedrock gives every aquatic both. A `swims` species with `walksOnLand = false` (cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish, squid, glow squid — `Creature.cpp:998–1113`) that is knocked onto a beach has `breathesAir = false`, so `dryOutSeconds`/the air counter will kill it, and no behaviour exists that would steer it back into the water. Worth a playtest: throw a fish onto sand and see whether it can ever recover.
10. **`Creature.cpp:668–674` (Bramble) · melee damage 3 · confidence: certain, and it is a *named divergence*, not a bug.** Bedrock's creeper has **no melee attack whatsoever** — its only damage is the blast. The comment states the reasoning ("a fuse that is cancelled still leaves something dangerous"). Recording it here only so nobody later "corrects" it toward the wiki and then wonders why a defused Bramble is harmless.
11. **`Creature.cpp:1122–1132` (Skeleton Horse / Zombie Horse) · sourced wrongly, and the blocker is gone · confidence: certain.** The comment says *"The reference only produces these from a lightning trap, which needs weather. Until then they are rare night grazers on open ground."* **Weather shipped at M27** and `Creatures::applyLightning` already exists (`Main.cpp:6632`). The skeleton trap is now buildable and the grassland spawn should retire.
12. **`Creature.cpp:559`/`:4412` (`separate`) · not a gap, and worth stating · confidence: certain.** We have a soft separation impulse and no entity cramming. **Bedrock has no entity cramming either** — `maxEntityCramming` is Java-exclusive. So "we are missing cramming" is not a finding, and adding it would be a divergence *away* from the reference.

**What I could not verify:** per-mob "version added" for Bedrock (it lives in 60 separate `HistoryTable` sections and I did not fetch them); exact Bedrock `movement` values for most species (the wiki's attribute table is tagged Java-exclusive — read `minecraft:movement.value` per entity file if a number matters); the Bedrock wandering-trader 40–60 minute despawn (the wiki flags its own claim `{{verify}}`); Bedrock demand-decay cadence for trade prices; the `sulfur_caves` biome and its mobs (camel husk, sulfur cube, parched), which are very recent and undocumented. I also did **not** build or run the game, per the brief, so every statement about our side is read from source rather than observed in play.

## 5. World generation, biomes, caves and structures

**Scope:** Overworld terrain shape, climate/biome selection, surface rules, caves, ores, decoration, structures and world-level generation facts — our `game/src/world/` generator measured against Bedrock Edition 1.21.x. Nether and End are out of scope and appear only where an overworld thing depends on them.

**Headline verdict:** The *terrain* half of this generator is genuinely close to Bedrock — the five climate fields, the spline stack, the 1.18 biome-box search, the surface-rule sequence and the `OreFeature` vein spindle are all the real architecture rather than an approximation of it, and a player walking the world will read it as the right game. The *content* half is nearly empty: there are exactly two structure generators in the whole codebase — trees and villages — and **no loot-table concept anywhere**, so the fifteen-odd structures Bedrock scatters across the overworld are not "partially done", they are absent, and half of them would still be empty shells the day they were placed. Three further absences are load-bearing well beyond worldgen — **and one of the three closed on 2026-08-19: lava's cave floor now generates** (`kLavaLevel = 6`), so **obsidian has a natural source** and only lava *lakes and springs* remain. The two still open: **no monster rooms or spawners** (so there is no dungeon loop), and **no aquifers, lakes, springs or carvers** (so caves are dry, sealed noise tunnels that never break the surface except through one 2D entrance field — though the floor of the deepest ones is now molten). The 96-block world height is a real constraint but a *second-order* one — it blocks four specific structures outright and squeezes cave layering, and everything else on the gap list can be built at the current height today.

> ✅ **The loot half of that verdict changed on 2026-08-18 and the rest did not.** `game/src/world/Loot.hpp`
> now exists — `Entry`/`Pool`/`Table` in three flat `constexpr` arrays under a kilobyte, `TableId` as the
> index, no heap during a roll — and villages place chests in weaponsmith, toolsmith and plain-house
> buildings. **That is slice 1 and it is small on purpose: three tables of roughly forty.** Dungeons,
> mineshafts, strongholds, ocean structures, desert pyramids, igloos, fishing and the twelve remaining
> village tables have none, and **there is still no structure other than a village to put a chest in**, so
> the sentence "half of them would be empty shells the day they were placed" is *still true of every
> structure on the list*. The system is no longer the blocker; the tables and the structures are.
>
> **Not played.** Nobody has opened one of these chests. The claim rests on a clean `/W4` build, a clean
> 45-second soak, `static_assert`s that check every stored pool total against the sum of its own weights,
> and four reviewers.

**Completeness estimate:** **Roughly 45% of Bedrock's overworld generation.** Split honestly: terrain shape and climate ≈ 85%; surface rules ≈ 60%; biome roster ≈ 55% (30 of ~54); caves ≈ 40%; ores ≈ 65%; vegetation and decoration ≈ 35%; structures ≈ 8% (villages and trees only, of ~20 generators); loot ≈ 0%; world-level services (border, world types, `/locate`) ≈ 5%.
