### 5.4 Errors and inconsistencies noticed while reading

1. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:358` (`veinHeight`) · the comment promises a triangle distribution and the code delivers a two-step piecewise-uniform one · confidence: certain.** The comment says *"the reference's `trapezoid` height provider with a zero plateau, which is just a triangle: the average of two uniform rolls"* — but the body computes `low = minY + range(lowSpan+1)`, `high = peakY + range(highSpan+1)` and then returns `range(2) == 0 ? low : high`. That is a coin flip between two **flat** uniform distributions, not their average. The result is flat within each half with a **step discontinuity at `peakY`**, and the density does not taper to nothing at either edge. Worked example — diamond (min 3, peak 6, max 17): the lower half is 4 values each at 0.125 probability, the upper half is 12 values each at 0.042, so y 3–5 is **3× denser** than y 7–17 with a hard cliff at y 6, where the reference would give a smooth ramp up and a smooth ramp down. Coal (8/26/70) gets a 2.4× step at y 26. The correct line is `return vein.minY + roll.range(lowSpan+1) + roll.range(highSpan+1)` scaled to the band, or literally the average of two rolls across the full span. **This is bug shape #1 and #3 from `CLAUDE.md` at once — a value derived somewhere other than the table that owns it, and a formula written from memory that came out wrong while still looking plausible — and it survived because "ore generates at roughly the right depth" is exactly the kind of thing a soak test cannot see.**
2. **`SYSTEM_MEMORY.md` → "World Generation" · says "twenty-seven biomes"; `Biome.hpp:31-62` has 30 · confidence: certain.** The `BiomeId` enum lists 30 entries before `Count`, and `Biome.cpp:47-330` has 30 rows. The three jungles (Jungle, SparseJungle, BambooJungle) were added after the doc was written. `RESEARCH.md` §15.9 and the task brief both repeat "27".
3. **`SYSTEM_MEMORY.md` → "Terrain Generation" (line ~1905 onward) is entirely pre-M20r and contradicts "World Generation" (line ~422) · confidence: certain.** It describes 7 biomes, 2D temperature/humidity selection with proximity weighting, biome `baseHeight`/`amplitude` fields, thresholded-noise ores, a hard deepslate cutoff at y 12 and bedrock at y ≤ 2. Every one of those is false of the current code: there are 30 biomes, selection is a 6-D box search, `Biome` has **no height fields at all** (deliberately), ores are placed spindle veins, deepslate is a probabilistic band 9–15, and bedrock is a probabilistic band 0–4. Its Structures and Villages subsections *are* current, which is what makes the section dangerous — it reads as authoritative. **A future session reading only that section will build the wrong thing.**
4. **`SYSTEM_MEMORY.md` → "Named divergences" · two block-availability claims are stale · confidence: certain.** (a) *"No cave biomes… need moss, dripstone and sculk, none of which exist"* — Moss Block, Moss Carpet, Dripstone Block, Pointed Dripstone, Sculk, Sculk Catalyst, Sculk Vein, Sculk Sensor and Sculk Shrieker **all exist in `Block.hpp` today**, along with azalea, cave vines, glow berries, dripleaf, spore blossom, rooted dirt and hanging roots. (b) *"Badlands has no banding… needs colours of terracotta we do not have"* — **all 16 dyed terracotta and all 16 glazed variants exist.** Both features are now ordinary table-and-rule work, not art-blocked, and the doc is actively discouraging work that is cheaper than it says.
5. **`Climate.cpp` vs `SYSTEM_MEMORY.md` → "World Generation" · two climate constants disagree · confidence: certain.** The doc states temperature wavelength 1536 and erosion gain 2.35; the code has **temperature wavelength 4096** and **erosion gain 1.75** (the latter lowered deliberately after a "too many peaks" playtest, which the doc records elsewhere without updating the number).
6. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:633-660` (seabed cover) · coral and sea pickles can generate in frozen and temperate shallows · confidence: likely.** The gate is `warm = biomeHasAny(biomeId, BiomeTag::Hot | BiomeTag::Sandy)`. `BiomeId::SnowyBeach` carries `Sandy` **and** `Frozen`; `BiomeId::Beach` carries `Sandy` with warmth 0.8; `BiomeId::Desert` carries both. So a submerged column off a *snowy* beach passes the "warm" test and can grow tube coral and sea pickles under ice. Bedrock puts coral in warm ocean only. The same `warm` flag is doing double duty for "what should the seabed be made of" (where including `Sandy` is correct and desirable) and "may coral grow here" (where it is not) — **this is exactly bug shape #2, a widened family predicate silently changing an unrelated caller.** The fix is a separate `BiomeTag::Ocean | BiomeTag::Hot` test for the coral branch.
7. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:662` and `:785` · a column whose surface is exactly `kSeaLevel` gets no vegetation of any kind · confidence: worth checking.** Ground cover requires `surface > kSeaLevel + 1` (≥ 26), sugar cane requires `surface == kSeaLevel + 1` (exactly 25), lily pads require `surface < kSeaLevel` (≤ 23). **y 24 falls through all three.** The water fill (`:625`) fills only `worldY <= surface`, so a y-24 column is dry land — a bare, plantless one-block band along every shoreline. Also worth noting that sugar cane can therefore *only ever* appear on that single y-25 shelf: no cane beside a river at altitude, ever, because there are no lakes and one sea level.
8. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:197` · `AncientDebris` is a Nether ore generating in the overworld · confidence: certain (the code) / deliberate (the intent).** It sits in `kOreVeins` at size 3, 3 attempts, y 3/8/16, `airDiscard 1.0`. In Bedrock it is Nether-only. Here it feeds `Smelting.cpp:23` → `ItemId::EmberiteScrap`, our netherite-tier equivalent, and since the Nether is permanently off the timeline this is **almost certainly the intended way to make that tier reachable**. Flagged so that a future session comparing against the wiki does not "fix" it. It should be written down in `DECISIONS.md` if it is not already.
9. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:197` · `OreVein` has no biome field, so emerald generates everywhere · confidence: certain.** 36 attempts per 32×32 column at y 10/46/62, in plains, on ocean floors and in deserts alike. Bedrock restricts emerald to 10 mountain biomes, which is the entire reason emerald means "you climbed a mountain". Same root cause blocks infested stone and the badlands gold bonus. See G5.9.
10. **`Block.hpp:125-126` · `Granite` and `Diorite` are unreachable · confidence: certain.** Neither appears as any biome's `patch` block in `Biome.cpp:47-330`, and there is no blob feature, so no generation path ever writes either one. They are in the block table, the item table and presumably the crafting tree, and they cannot be obtained. `Andesite` escapes this only because Stony Peaks names it as a patch. See G5.6.
11. **`Structures.cpp:279-291` · `DarkOakLog` and `AcaciaLog` are unreachable · confidence: certain.** `buildTree` picks between `Log`, `BirchLog`, `SpruceLog` and `JungleLog` only. `BiomeId::Savanna` (`TreeShape::Round`) grows oak; `BiomeId::DenseForest`, our dark-forest stand-in, also grows oak. Both wood families exist as blocks with full plank/stair/slab chains and neither can be obtained in survival. See G5.11.
12. **`Structures.cpp` vs `TerrainGenerator.cpp:47` · two different `kSteepDrop` values in two files · confidence: worth checking.** The surface rule uses `kSteepDrop = 2` (matching Bedrock's "vertical gradient of the north and south side > 2"); the tree gate uses a local `kSteepDrop = 4`. Two constants with the same name meaning "how steep is too steep" in two files is the exact shape `CLAUDE.md`'s opening box warns about. It is plausibly deliberate — a tree wants a laxer test than a bare-rock rule — but if so the local one should be named `kTreeSlopeLimit` and say why.
13. **`TerrainGenerator.cpp:~655` · kelp is a single block and never a column · confidence: certain.** One `BlockId::Kelp` is written at `surface + 1` and nothing grows above it. In Bedrock kelp grows a stalk to within a few blocks of the surface, which is most of what makes a cold ocean read as an ocean. Trivial to fix (a 1–N loop) and worth doing with G5.8.
14. ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-19 — lava now generates, so `BlockId::Obsidian` has a natural source.** The original entry read: *"No generation path writes lava, so `BlockId::Obsidian` has no natural source · confidence: certain. Grepped `TerrainGenerator.cpp`, `Structures.cpp`, `Village.cpp` and `Biome.cpp` for `Lava`: zero hits."* That was correct when measured. A flood layer at `kLavaLevel = 6` landed on 2026-08-19, filling carver-emptied cells at or below y 6. **Nothing downstream of obsidian is blocked by generation any more.** Lava lakes and springs are still absent — *refuted by any lava write outside the flood layer.* See G5.3.
15. **`Climate.cpp:160` · the continentalness spline extrapolates linearly below its first control point (−1.10) · confidence: worth checking, by design.** The comment states linear extrapolation rather than clamping is deliberate. It matters here because Bedrock's mushroom-fields band is continentalness −1.2…−1.05, i.e. **partly outside the defined range**, so if G5.10 adds mushroom fields the height it produces will come from extrapolation rather than from a control point. Add an eighth spline point rather than trusting the extrapolation.

## 6. Blocks, items and their behaviour

**Scope:** Overworld only — the block table, the item catalogue and the *mechanisms* that make a block or item behave, measured against Bedrock Edition; Nether/End content is noted in one line where an overworld system needs it and is otherwise out of scope, as is art.

**Headline verdict:** The roster is close to finished and the behaviour layer is not. **3,309 block ids at the last probe, capped at 3,584 by a live `static_assert` — see the count note below** — and 1,343 catalogue entries (*unverified — no constant states this and it has not been re-measured*) cover almost every overworld family Bedrock has — amethyst, the full copper set including bulbs and grates, sculk, deepslate, tuff, dripstone, moss/azalea/dripleaf/cave-vines, mud and mangrove, cherry, bamboo blocks, powder snow, scaffolding, candles, suspicious sand and gravel, chiseled bookshelf — and the table-driven scheme genuinely delivers what it promises: a new block is one row in `kExtraBlocks` plus a parent in `shapedParent`. The gap is that **most of those rows have nowhere to put a behaviour**. ⚠️ **The sentence that used to follow is dead and its replacement matters:** *"The engine has exactly one random-tick consumer — crops — so nothing in the world grows, spreads, decays, melts, oxidises or dies; the sampler at `World.cpp:670` filters to farmland/crop/stem/wart and `continue`s on everything else."* **That closed on 2026-08-19** — `World.cpp` `randomTicks` also names grass, mycelium, ice, snow layers, budding amethyst, saplings, leaf blocks, pointed dripstone and any copper with a next weathering stage, held by four `static_assert`s; **vines are the one item on the original unlock list still absent.** The other big structural holes are one per system rather than one per block: no enchantment data on a stack, no map item that renders, one flammability bit where Bedrock has two numbers, friction implemented for ice and nothing else, and contact damage implemented for cactus and nothing else.

> **The block-id count, what it is bracketed to, and why an earlier version of this note was wrong — 2026-08-19 10:20.**
> The last *probe-measured* value is **3,309** (`Block.hpp` `kBlockIdCount`, compile-time `Show<N>`
> probe at ~06:00 on 2026-08-19; the **2,871** this section used to carry was two roster rounds
> stale, and its `SYSTEM_MEMORY.md:2938` citation pointed at a blank line in the culling section).
>
> ⚠️ **An earlier version of this note, written 10:09 today, said "≥ 3,339" and that is impossible in
> a tree that builds. It is left here as the worked example, because the mistake is the useful part.**
> The reasoning was: two runs are readable without a probe — `BeeNestRunFirst..Last` is
> `kBeehiveHoneyLevels * 4` = **6 × 4 = 24** ids, and `FarmlandMoistureRunFirst..Last` is
> `kFarmlandPartialMoistureLevels` = `kFarmlandMoistureLevels − 2` = **6** ids, *not* 8 (levels 0 and
> 7 already had ids — the storage-domain-versus-range trap, and `Block.hpp` says so at the constant)
> — therefore 3,309 + 24 + 6 = 3,339. **Both run sizes are right and the sum is still wrong**,
> because it assumed the 06:00 probe predated both runs, and nothing was checked that could say so.
> That is one unsourced number replaced by another, which this repository's house rule forbids.
>
> **What settles it without a build — and this paragraph has itself been overtaken once, which is the
> point.** `game/src/item/Mining.hpp` builds `kMiningRows` in 256-id chunks and a `static_assert`
> bounds `kBlockIdCount` against the chunks actually written. **At 10:20 that read
> `static_assert(kMiningChunkCount == 13)` over thirteen hand-written pointers, giving a ceiling of
> 3,328 and a bracket of [3,073 … 3,328]** — enough to prove the 3,339 figure impossible, which is
> what it was used for. ✅ **At 10:23:32 the file changed.** The constant was split in two:
> `kMiningChunkCount` (how many the enum *needs*, derived) and `kMiningChunkCapacity` (how many are
> *written*, now 14), the assert became `kMiningChunkCount <= kMiningChunkCapacity`, and a second
> assert pins the capacity against the chunks actually written so raising one number alone cannot
> silence it. **The ceiling is now 3,584 and the headroom is ~275 ids, not 19.**
> **Use 3,309 as the working figure and 3,584 as the hard ceiling.**
>
> ⭐ **That second assert was itself rewritten within the hour, and it is the best `constexpr`
> lesson of the day.** Its first form compared pointers —
> `kMiningChunks[kMiningChunkCapacity - 1] == &kMiningChunk13`. That is sound C++ on paper (both
> operands address one object with static storage duration), but **pointer identity inside a constant
> expression is exactly where MSVC is narrowest**, and it is the kind of thing that compiles under one
> toolset and not the next. The replacement, `chunkPointersMapToTheirBases()`, **compares the values
> the pointers yield instead** — it walks every chunk the table can reach and checks row 0 against the
> row that base derives, all four fields rather than one, because `tier` alone collides freely. It
> catches both failures the capacity split could introduce: a **null slot** (dereferencing one is
> ill-formed in a constant expression, so raising the capacity without adding the pointer stops the
> build) and a **mis-wired slot**. It is non-vacuous by construction, and it reuses character for
> character the expression `makeMiningRows` already evaluates — **so it cannot fail for a reason that
> would not also have broken the table itself.** That last property is the whole argument for the
> form, and it is the one to copy: *an assert is safe when the compiler is already known to evaluate
> its exact expression elsewhere*, not when it merely looks tame.
>
> **Two things follow that are worth more than the number.** First, **the ~19-id margin that made
> this urgent is gone** — a spare chunk is now landable ahead of need, and it costs nothing while
> unused because `makeMiningChunk`'s loop stops at `kBlockIdCount` and so does `makeMiningRows`.
> Second, **a derived count with a hand-written list behind it is not derived** — the array size
> followed the enum and the initialiser did not, and only a `static_assert` closed the gap. **That is
> the transferable lesson and it now has a worked repair:** `Mining.hpp` names the *need* and the
> *supply* as two constants and asserts one against the other, plus a control pinning the supply to
> the actual pointer list — because an assert that compares one side of a derivation against itself
> proves nothing (bug shape #11). Copy that arrangement, not the number.
> **What would make this note false:** a re-probe, another chunk appearing in `Mining.hpp`, or any run
> appended after 10:08 today (`Block.hpp` was last written at **10:08:23**). `kLastBlock` is
> `BlockId::FarmlandMoistureRunLast`, so the tail run is where to look.

**Completeness estimate:**
- **Roster coverage ≈ 88%** of Bedrock's overworld blocks and ≈ 85% of its overworld items. Named absences: decorated pots, ~~bee nest~~ (**landed 2026-08-19 as a real 24-id run with its own honey levels — see the Tier 1 refill in §0.5 for the one call site that stops it filling**), turtle egg, pink petals, torchflower/pitcher plant, copper door/trapdoor, and everything from 1.21 onward (crafter, trial spawner, vault, heavy core, pale garden, firefly bush, leaf litter, copper chest/golem). Items: bundles, writable book, horse armour, wolf armour, smithing templates/armour trims, spectral arrow, cake.
- **Behaviour coverage ≈ 45%.** Weighted by mechanism rather than by id: 8 of the ~20 block mechanisms Bedrock runs are Full, 6 Partial, 6 Absent. Weighted by *id*, roughly **1,150–1,300 ids (35–40% of ≥ 3,339) are inert** — they place, break, drop, occlude and blast correctly and do nothing else. ⚠️ **The percentage moved because the denominator did, not because anything was built:** this line divided by **2,871** while the headline above it said 3,309, so the section contradicted itself by 438 ids. The numerator is unchanged and is itself an estimate. That figure is dominated by the 640 cut shapes and the 41-piece redstone kit, both of which are inert *by design*, so the honest number for "inert and shouldn't be" is closer to **160–200 ids** (§6.4).

### 6.3 Gap detail

#### ✅ G6.1 — Random ticks reach only crops · M · ~~P0~~ · CLOSED 2026-08-19
- **Bedrock behaviour:** `randomTickSpeed` defaults to **1** in Bedrock (3 in Java), giving a mean of **204.8 s per block**. On each selection the block runs its own rule. Overworld consumers: grass/mycelium spread and death, leaf decay, ice/snow melt, water freeze, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp, vines, cave vines, saplings, mushrooms, turtle eggs, moss, sculk, copper oxidation, coral death, and crops. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tick](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tick)
- **What we have:** the sampler is correct and the rate is *exactly* right — `Farming.hpp:124` sets 8 samples per 32³ chunk per 50 ms tick, which is 4096 ticks = 204.8 s mean per cell, and the comment at `Farming.hpp:120–124` names Bedrock's figure explicitly. But `World.cpp:679–683` reads the sampled cell and `continue`s unless it is farmland, a crop, a stem or nether wart. **There is one consumer.**
- **What must be built:** turn the filter into a dispatch. Add a `constexpr bool ticksRandomly(BlockId)` beside `isFalling` in `Block.hpp` and a `World::randomTick(glm::ivec3, BlockId)` that switches on family, with `growOne` becoming the crop case. The predicate is what stops the sampler paying a switch cost on every cell of stone. Then each rule below is one case.
- **Numbers that matter:** 204.8 s mean interval (already correct — **do not change `kRandomTicksPerChunkPerTick`**, it is derived from `Chunk::kSize = 32`, and `Chunk.hpp:18` is the number it depends on). Grass spread: source needs light ≥ 9 above it, target dirt needs light ≥ 4 above it, 3×5×3 volume, up to 4 attempts per tick. Grass death: covered by opacity ≥ 2 or a fluid. Leaf decay: > 4 taxicab blocks from a log in Bedrock (6 in Java `[JE]`), player-placed leaves persistent. Ice melts at block light ≥ 12; snow layers melt at block light ≥ 12, one layer at a time in Bedrock (all at once `[JE]`). Sugar cane and cactus: +1 height per **16** random ticks, max 3. Bamboo: light ≥ 9 at the tip, max 12–16. Vines: 25% per tick, needs < 4 vine blocks in a 9×9×3 box. Cave vines: 10% per tick to extend, 11% of new segments bear berries. Mushrooms: 4% per tick, blocked if ≥ 5 mushrooms in a 9×9×3 box. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Grass_Block](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Grass_Block), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Leaves](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Leaves), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sugar_Cane](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sugar_Cane), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bamboo](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bamboo), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Vines](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Vines)
- **Risks / dependencies:** every rule below reads neighbours, and the sampler runs on the main thread inside a budget check — keep each case O(small) and let the budget cut it off. Grass spread and leaf decay both call `setBlock`, which flags a chunk modified and therefore writes it to disk; a bad rule will permanently pollute saves. That is the exact trap `CLAUDE.md` box item 14 records, and `kChunkFormatVersion` is the lever.

#### G6.2 — No enchantment model · L · P0
- **Bedrock behaviour:** enchantments are per-stack data with a level; the table costs 1–3 levels + lapis and offers three tiers driven by bookshelf count (15 shelves = level 30). Efficiency, Fortune, Silk Touch, Unbreaking, Protection, Sharpness, Power, Feather Falling, Mending, Looting are the load-bearing ones. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Enchanting](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Enchanting)
- **What we have:** the string "enchant" appears twice in `Item.hpp` and both are the `EnchantingTable` block item. `ItemStack` is `{ItemId item; int count; int damage;}` (`Item.hpp:1578`) with no room for anything else. The table is a block id with light 7 (`Block.hpp:6037`) and a cutout model; right-clicking it is not in `isInteractive` (`Block.hpp:2824`), so it does nothing at all. Bookshelves exist (`isFlammable`, village libraries) with no relationship to it.
- **What must be built:** a bitfield or small fixed array on `ItemStack`, a `constexpr` enchantment table (id → max level, applicable tool kinds, weight), a lapis+levels cost model, a screen, and read hooks in `Mining.hpp` `breakSeconds` (Efficiency), `Mining.hpp` `canHarvest` (Silk Touch; the old `Tool.cpp` `yieldsDrop` spelling is gone), `dropCountForBlock` (Fortune), the durability decrement path (Unbreaking/Mending), and armour damage (Protection).
- **Numbers that matter:** Efficiency adds `level² + 1` to tool speed. Fortune III on coal/diamond/emerald/lapis/redstone: weighted 1/1/2/3/4 multiplier. Unbreaking: durability loss chance `1/(level+1)` for tools, `60+40/(level+1)` % for armour. Protection: 4% damage reduction per point, capped at 80%.
- **Risks / dependencies:** **this changes the save format** — `ItemStack` is serialised into chests, the player and dropped entities. It also collides with the `damage`-as-stowbox-identity overload already flagged in §4.1/§4.2 of this audit; widening the stack is the natural moment to give stowbox contents their own field instead. This is the largest single item in the section and it unblocks a lot of the survival loop, so **hand the whole system to the survival section** rather than treating it as a catalogue job.

#### ✅ G6.3 — Saplings never grow · S · ~~P0~~ · CLOSED 2026-08-19
- **Bedrock behaviour:** a sapling needs light ≥ 9 at the block above and advances a stage per random tick; two stages then a tree. Dark oak requires a 2×2; spruce and jungle optionally form giants. Bone meal skips the light requirement. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Oak_Sapling](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Oak_Sapling)
- **What we have (updated 2026-08-19):** six sapling ids marked `natural`; they place, break and drop. `World.cpp` `growSaplingAt` is the rule, reached from **both** the random tick and `applyBoneMeal`, so the two-by-two dark-oak rule has one owner. `randomTicks` names `farming::isSapling`, held by a `static_assert`.
- ~~**What must be built:** a random-tick case that checks light ≥ 9, space above, and calls the existing tree generator from `Structures.cpp` at a world position rather than into a chunk buffer; plus a bone-meal case.~~ **Built 2026-08-19.** The only work left here is the missing sapling ids: cherry, mangrove propagule, bamboo shoot.
- **Numbers that matter:** light ≥ 9 above; space checks per species (oak 5 clear above a 3×3, birch 6, spruce 6 within 5×5, acacia 6, cherry 8, giant spruce 14, giant jungle 11); bone meal has a 45% chance per use to advance a stage.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the tree generator currently writes into a chunk under generation, where neighbours do not exist. Growing a tree in a *loaded* world must go through `setBlock` and cross chunk borders — that is the same purity boundary `CLAUDE.md` protects, so keep it "compute the block list, then apply it" rather than letting the generator mutate the world.

#### G6.4 — Movement and contact behaviour has no general mechanism · M · P1
- **Bedrock behaviour:** cobweb slows to ~25% and negates fall damage (breakable with a sword, 2 durability). Scaffolding is climbed by holding jump, descended by sneak, and extends 6 blocks horizontally in Bedrock (7 `[JE]`). Powder snow sinks entities, starts freezing after **140 ticks (7 s)** then deals 1 HP per 40 ticks, is walkable in leather boots, and extinguishes fire. Sweet berry bush: ~34% speed and 1 HP/0.5 s while moving. Magma block: 1 HP/0.5 s, avoided by sneaking. Campfire: 1 HP/0.5 s. Pointed dripstone: landing on a stalagmite deals `ceil(fallDistance × 2 − 2)`. Honey block: ~2.5 m/s walk, jump cut to ~3/16 block, slides down walls, 80% fall-damage reduction. Hay bale also ×0.2; bed ×0.5. Slime block negates fall damage entirely and bounces at ~0.8 unless sneaking. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cobweb](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cobweb), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powder_Snow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powder_Snow), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Scaffolding](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Scaffolding), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sweet_Berry_Bush](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sweet_Berry_Bush), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Honey_Block](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Honey_Block), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Damage](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Damage)
- **What we have:** three separate one-off answers instead of one table. `slipperiness` (`Block.hpp:6320`) returns a float but only for the three ice ids. `isSticky` (`Block.hpp:6254`) is a boolean for honey + honeycomb, consumed as a single `kStickySpeedScale` at `Player.cpp:617`. The slime bounce is a hard-coded id comparison at `Player.cpp:842`. Contact damage is a single `onCactus` bool at `Player.cpp:223`. Cobweb, powder snow, scaffolding and berry bush appear only in `Tool.cpp` (hardness) and the texture atlas.
- **What must be built:** one `constexpr` struct per block — `BlockMotion { float slipperiness; float speedScale; float fallDamageScale; bool bounces; bool climbable; int contactDamage; }` — beside `slipperiness` in `Block.hpp`, with the existing four call sites reading fields off it. That is one row per hazard block thereafter, which is the scheme the rest of the file already uses. Widen `isClimbable` (`Block.hpp:3337`) to include scaffolding at the same time.
- **Numbers that matter:** default slipperiness 0.6; ice/packed/frosted 0.98; blue ice 0.989; slime 0.8. Cobweb ×0.25 movement, free-fall 0.078 blocks/s. Berry bush ×0.34 + 1 HP/0.5 s while moving. Freezing: 140 ticks to start, 1 HP per 40 ticks, `TicksFrozen` +1/tick inside and −2/tick outside, cap 140. Fall-damage multipliers: hay 0.2, honey 0.2, bed 0.5, slime/cobweb/powder snow/berry bush 0.0.
- **Risks / dependencies:** `surfaceMotion` (`Player.cpp:523`) derives acceleration from slipperiness as `0.91 × s` with a `0.6/s` ratio — feeding it 0.8 for slime is safe, but feeding it a *speed* scale is not, which is precisely why honey was implemented as a separate multiplier. Keep the two fields distinct. Creature movement (`Creature.cpp`) reads none of this and will need the same hooks or mobs will walk on ice like stone.

#### G6.5 — Waterlogging gated to Cross shapes · S · P1
- **Bedrock behaviour:** Bedrock does not use Java's per-block `waterlogged` boolean; every position has an independent **liquid layer** behind the block layer, and a per-block capability decides whether the liquid shows. Waterloggable overworld blocks include all slabs, stairs, fences, gates, walls, trapdoors, panes, iron bars, ladders, signs and hanging signs, chains, lanterns, conduit, sea pickle, kelp, coral and coral fans, campfire, scaffolding, mangrove roots, pointed dripstone, big and small dripleaf, lightning rod, copper grate and rails. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Waterlogging](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Waterlogging)
- **What we have:** **the harder half is already built and it is built the Bedrock way.** `Chunk.hpp:67–98` is one bit per cell across the whole 32³ chunk — a real second layer, not a per-block state. The gate is `canWaterlog` at `Block.hpp:6241`, which is `blockShape(id) == BlockShape::Cross` and nothing else, with two `static_assert`s pinning that. The header states the reason: a stair sharing a cell with water "fights that water for the same depth values and shimmers", and placing a real block into a source should destroy it.
- **What must be built:** widen `canWaterlog` to the shape families that are already thin — `Slab` (lower half only), `Stairs`, `Fence`, `Wall`, `Gate`, `Pane`, `Trapdoor`, `Ladder`, `Sign`, plus named ids for lantern, chain, campfire, scaffolding, pointed dripstone, lightning rod, copper grate. Then fix the reason it was excluded: the mesher must draw the water surface at a fixed full-cell height inside a waterlogged non-Cross block rather than deriving a depth, and `occludesFace` (`Block.hpp:5941`) must not let the block cull the water quad. Update the two `static_assert`s so they still assert something true.
- **Numbers that matter:** none — this is structural. Note that our water uses 8 levels (`kMaxWaterLevel = 7`, `Block.hpp:2833`); a waterlogged cell must always render and behave as a **source**, which is what removes the shimmer.
- **Risks / dependencies:** bug shape #6 — a blended water fragment inside a waterlogged stair will write depth and reject the stair's own geometry behind it. Check the blend pass before believing the visual result.

#### G6.6 — Flammability is one bit where Bedrock has two numbers · S · P2
- **Bedrock behaviour:** each flammable block carries **(encouragement, flammability)** = (how easily fire spreads *to* it, how fast it is consumed). Logs/wood/coal block **5/5**; planks and wooden stairs/slabs/fences/gates, composter, beehive, mangrove roots **5/20**; carpet **30/60** (Bedrock; 60/20 `[JE]`); cave vines 15/60; TNT and vines 15/100; bookshelf and lectern 30/20; leaves and wool **30/60**; hay bale **60/20**; bamboo and scaffolding 60/60; short/tall grass, ferns, dead bush, two-block flowers **60/100**. Ignition degree is `(maxNeighbourFlammability + 7·difficulty + 40) / (age + 30)`, halved in humid biomes. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire)
- **What we have:** `isFlammable` (`Block.hpp:6381`) returns a single `bool`, and the header says so outright: *"we need only the first, because ours does not model how fast a block is consumed."* Spread is a flat 25% per neighbour per pass and burnout a flat 40% (`World.cpp:68–69`). It is a genuinely good shape test — every Cross block burns, so new flowers are covered automatically — and it forwards through `shapedParent`, so 640 cut shapes are free.
- **What must be built:** replace the boolean with `constexpr FireOdds fireOdds(BlockId)` returning `{uint8_t ignite; uint8_t burn;}` and keep `isFlammable(id)` as `fireOdds(id).ignite > 0` so no existing caller changes. Then `World.cpp:739` rolls against `ignite` instead of the flat 25, and the burn-away pass rolls against `burn`.
- **Numbers that matter:** the pairs above; also that Bedrock fire runs off random ticks, so its spread rate scales with `randomTickSpeed`, and the `dofiretick` gamerule halts all fire updates.
- **Risks / dependencies:** `blastResistance` uses `isFlammable` as its "the woods" fall-through — keep the boolean's meaning identical or every wooden block's blast resistance moves. This is bug shape #2: widening a family predicate kills the early-outs behind it. *(Citation made symbolic 2026-08-19: this read `Explosion.cpp:436`, which is wrong twice over — `Explosion.cpp` is 222 lines, and `blastResistance` is not in it. It is a `constexpr` table in `Block.hpp`; `Explosion.cpp` says so in a comment above the one place it is read, the intensity loop.)*

#### G6.7 — Filled maps · L · P1
- **Bedrock behaviour:** an empty map is filled on use, centred on a 128×128-block region at scale 0, expandable to 1:16 (2048×2048) through four zoom levels on a cartography table. It renders as an item-in-hand and in a frame, with a player marker. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Map](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Map)
- **What we have:** `ItemId::EmptyMap` (`Item.hpp:342`), craftable (`Recipe.cpp` only reference), plus `CartographyTable` and `Compass` as similarly inert items. No filled-map id, no per-map pixel store, no rendering path.
- **What must be built:** a map-data store keyed by map id (top block colour per column, sampled as chunks load), a `FilledMap` item whose `damage` field indexes it, a HUD/held rendering path, and save/load. The block-colour source already exists — `Material.hpp:120` `materialFamilyFor` and the texture layer table give a per-block average colour cheaply.
- **Numbers that matter:** 128×128 pixels at scale 0; 1 pixel per block at scale 0, 1 per 2/4/8/16 blocks at scales 1–4; 4 shade levels per colour driven by relative height.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the only item in this section that needs new *rendering*, which is why it is L. It is also the highest-visibility single feature here — an "I can see where I've been" moment.

#### ✅ G6.8 — Leaf decay, ice melt, snow melt · XS each · ~~P1~~ · CLOSED 2026-08-19
- **Bedrock behaviour:** non-persistent leaves decay when more than **4** taxicab blocks from a log (6 `[JE]`); player-placed leaves are persistent. Ice melts to water on a random tick at **block light ≥ 12** (sky light ignored). Snow layers melt at block light ≥ 12, one layer at a time in Bedrock, and Bedrock additionally melts snow in non-snow biomes regardless of light. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Leaves](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Leaves), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Ice](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Ice), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Snow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Snow)
- **What we have (updated 2026-08-19):** the *formation* half was always done and done well — `Main.cpp` accumulates snow layers up the `snowLayerAt` run and freezes water sources to ice, both gated on open sky and block light < 12, with per-column biome sampling so a snow line does not smear. **All three melt/decay rules now exist too.** Leaf decay is `World.cpp` `decayLeafIfOrphaned`, reached from the random tick *and* from a neighbour change, with `leafHasWoodNearby` doing a **flood fill through leaves** bounded by `farming::kLeafDecayReach = 4` and `farming::leafKeeper` naming logs and bark. Ice and snow melt in the `Ice`/`isSnowLayer` random-tick branch, reading `blockLightAt` and never sky light, threshold > 11, packed and blue ice excluded by id, snow one layer at a time. Bedrock's persistence bit is a real per-cell flag (`Chunk.hpp`, beside `m_waterlogged`) and is **saved** — `WorldStore.cpp` calls it out as a version 6 file field.
- ~~**What must be built:** three random-tick cases (G6.1). Leaves additionally need a persistent flag — the cheapest place is a parallel bit array beside `m_waterlogged` in `Chunk.hpp`~~ **Built 2026-08-19, and by exactly that route.** **One half is deliberately still absent:** Bedrock also melts snow in any non-snowy biome regardless of light, which needs a biome the world can be asked for at a point; the code omits it and says so rather than guessing.
- **Numbers that matter:** decay distance 4 (Bedrock); melt threshold block light ≥ 12; the freeze side already uses < 12 and matches.
- ~~**Risks / dependencies:** without melt, snow and ice are **monotonic**~~ — resolved. The general warning still stands for whatever comes next: these rules call `setBlock`, which marks a chunk modified and therefore writes it to disk, so a wrong rule permanently pollutes saves. `kChunkFormatVersion` is the lever (`CLAUDE.md` box item 7).

#### G6.9 — Copper oxidation and waxing · S · P2
- **Bedrock behaviour:** oxidation depends **only on random ticks** — rain, water and cover are irrelevant. Each tick a copper block has a **64/1125** chance (~5%/min) to enter pre-oxidation; it then scans non-waxed copper within taxicab 4, refuses if any neighbour is *less* oxidised, and otherwise oxidises with probability `m·c²` where `c = (b+1)/(a+1)` and `m = 0.75` if unoxidised else 1. Honeycomb waxes; an axe strips wax and scrapes one stage back. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Oxidation](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Oxidation) *(the formula is documented for Java; Bedrock parity assumed)*
- **What we have — ✅ essentially all of it; this bullet and the one below it were stale, corrected 2026-08-19 11:56.** The roster is plain/exposed/weathered/oxidised × plain/cut/chiseled/grate/bulb plus waxed forms, ~40 ids, **but it is not "the whole roster": `CopperDoor` and `CopperTrapdoor` measure 0 in `Block.hpp`, in any form.** `isCopperBulb` and `isCopperBulbLit` derive the bulb's 15/12/8/4 light from oxidation-stage arithmetic. **And there is now a whole `world/Copper.hpp`** — 18 `constexpr` functions including `stageOf`, `atStage`, `weathered`, `scraped`, `waxedForm`, `unwaxedForm`, `oxidationChancePpm`, `octahedronCells`, and three self-checks (`runsWellFormed`, `runsDisjoint`, `everyCopperPassSwept`). ⚠️ *The old text here claimed `ExposedCopper` and `WeatheredCopper` appear nowhere outside `Block.hpp` — that is false: each appears 9 times in `Copper.hpp`.*
- **What must be built — ✅ CLOSED; the old list described work that is done.** It called for `oxidisedForm`/`waxedForm`/`scrapedForm`, a random-tick case, and two `Main.cpp` interaction cases. **All present.** ⓪ **Two of the three names were simply wrong, which is why a token search "confirmed" the gap**: the functions are `weathered()` and `scraped()`, not `oxidisedForm`/`scrapedForm` — searching the doc's own spelling returns 0 in every file while the real ones return 15 and 6 in `Copper.hpp`. Player interactions are live in `Main.cpp` (`unwaxedForm`, `scraped`, `waxedForm` — axe strips wax, axe scrapes a stage, honeycomb waxes), and **passive oxidation is wired**: `World.cpp` carries 16 `copper::` references beside 13 `randomTick` mentions, calling `weathered()` and `oxidationChancePpm`. *Probes landed 4 of 5; invented control name 0.* **What genuinely remains: the copper door and trapdoor (0 ids), the copper bulb's toggle, and the eight waxed stair/slab family rows below.** *Falsifier: `Copper.hpp` disappearing, or `copper::` returning 0 in `World.cpp`.*
- ❗ **The waxed stair/slab unblock is EIGHT ROWS IN TWO EXISTING TABLES, not eight new ids — and the distinction is the whole risk profile.** `WaxedCutCopper`, `WaxedExposedCutCopper`, `WaxedWeatheredCutCopper` and `WaxedOxidizedCutCopper` **all already exist** as enumerators. What is missing is family rows: `kStairFamilies` and `kSlabFamilies` each list the **four bare** cut coppers as parents (`CutCopper`, `ExposedCutCopper`, `WeatheredCutCopper`, `OxidizedCutCopper`) **and no waxed form**. So the work is four rows in each table — **no new enumerators, no mid-enum renumbering, no chunk-format bump, no save invalidation.** *Measured 2026-08-19; falsified by any `Waxed*CutCopper` appearing in either family table.* **And a rule the copper audit paid for: a recipe is blocked by its INPUTS as well as its output** — one waxed chiseled stage stays unwritable even though its output id exists, because the reference shape consumes a waxed cut copper *slab*. **Counting only outputs undercounts the blockers.**
- **Numbers that matter:** 64/1125 per random tick; taxicab radius 4; `m = 0.75` for the unoxidised → exposed step, 1.0 thereafter.
- **Risks / dependencies:** none structural — this is the cheapest large-id-count win in the section, and it makes honeycomb (already obtainable) worth something.

#### G6.10 — Amethyst growth, sculk spreading, sponge absorption · S each · P2/P3
- **Bedrock behaviour:** budding amethyst grows a small bud on any of its six faces on a random tick, advancing small → medium → large → cluster; budding amethyst itself is unobtainable (drops nothing even with Silk Touch). A sculk catalyst blooms when a mob dies within **10 blocks** (Bedrock; 8 `[JE]`), converting 1 XP into 1 charge and 1 sculk block, with a **9%** chance per discharge of a sculk sensor and **1%** of a shrieker, suppressed if ≥ 2 already exist in a 9×3×9 box. A sponge flood-fills water out to taxicab 7 and becomes a wet sponge. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Amethyst_Cluster](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Amethyst_Cluster), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sculk_Catalyst](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sculk_Catalyst), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sponge](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sponge)
- **What we have:** `BuddingAmethyst`, `SmallAmethystBud`, `MediumAmethystBud`, `LargeAmethystBud` and `AmethystCluster` all exist with correct light levels (1/2/4/5, `Block.hpp:6029–6033, 6061`); `BuddingAmethyst` and `AmethystCluster` appear nowhere outside `Block.hpp`. `Sculk`, `SculkVein`, `SculkCatalyst`, `SculkSensor`, `SculkShrieker` exist with correct light (catalyst 6, sensor 1) and appear only in the texture atlas, the creative catalogue (`Main.cpp:2508`) and `Explosion.cpp`. `Sponge`/`WetSponge` exist, smelt into each other (`Smelting.cpp:26`) and never touch water.

Sponge: taxicab 7, ~65 water blocks *(the current wiki text is internally inconsistent on this cap — verify before pinning the number)*.

A conduit needs a prismarine/sea-lantern frame and grants conduit power in a range set by frame size (up to 96 blocks at 42 frame blocks). #### G6.13 — Bundles, decorated pots, brushing · M · P3
- **Bedrock behaviour:** a bundle holds 64 "weight" across mixed item types and is opened in the inventory. A decorated pot is crafted from 4 bricks and/or sherds, holds one stack, and shatters into its sherds when broken without a tool. Suspicious sand/gravel is revealed by a brush and drops a loot item; both have hardness 0.25. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bundle](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bundle), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Decorated_Pot](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Decorated_Pot), [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Brush](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Brush)
- **What we have:** `SuspiciousSand` and `SuspiciousGravel` exist as blocks (referenced only in `Explosion.cpp`). 23 pottery sherd items exist (`Item.hpp:24`, `:683` `kPotterySherdNames`) with sprites and no use whatsoever. `Brush` exists as an item. **No bundle id and no decorated pot id.**
- **What must be built:** the decorated pot is the cheapest — a block id, a shapeless recipe over 4 sherds/bricks, one stack of storage in the existing `chests` map, and a break rule that returns the sherds. Brushing needs a held-use timer and a loot table on the two suspicious blocks. The bundle needs a new stack-of-stacks container type, which is the only genuinely new data shape here.

#### G6.14 — Model coverage holes · informational · P3
- **What `check-models.ps1` proves:** it runs the game once with `block_probe=1`, dumps every drawn block's geometry, and compares it against the reference's `models/block/*.json`. **It runs three checks, not one** — the *union extent* at half-a-texel tolerance; a *box count* for `Model` blocks only; and every *face rectangle* read out of `postModel` in `Block.hpp` against the `uv` the reference states. (Search `check-models.ps1` for `extent`, `uv` and `facetemplate`; its header comment names all three.)
- **Current reading (2026-08-19, from `SYSTEM_MEMORY.md`'s "Every block is checked against the reference's own model" — not re-run here, the machine is under load):** **3230 blocks drawn, 2629 matched a reference model and agree, 0 disagree, 271 with no model.** Beside the extents: **359 `Model` blocks compared box for box, 0 disagreeing on how many**, and **95 face rectangles compared against the reference `uv`, 0 disagreeing**.
- ⚠️ **The old "3,186 drawn / 1,792 matched / 1,370 no model" figure that stood here until 2026-08-19 is superseded, and quoting it back would understate coverage by 837 blocks.** It was also measured by a *weaker* tool: until it gained the box count and the `uv` comparison it compared **union extents alone**, which passed a flower pot whose two X walls carried the lid's rect and a scaffolding missing its four top rails. **Its fault count went 1792/0 → 2539/275 → 2629/0 — the 275 was the tool ceasing to be blind, not the geometry getting worse.** Do not read a rising fault count here as a regression.
- **Where the holes are now:** the residue is **271**, not 1,370 — **202** blocks the reference draws as a block entity and ships no geometry for, **69** it ships only as a single face template, and **0** that we failed to find a model for at all. The old worry in this entry — *"a newly added model-shaped block silently lands in the unmeasured bucket"* — is largely closed by that **0 unfound**, because the tool now follows variants and templates and names a reason for every block it cannot check. **Still honest rather than clean:** 29 boxes in `postModel` could not be read statically (they sit behind a switch, a loop or a variable) and 5 more had no element in the same place to compare against; **neither group is counted as agreeing**, which is the correct way round.

### 6.5 Errors and inconsistencies noticed while reading

- **`Block.hpp:6320` `slipperiness`** · The doc comment two lines above names the reference's values *"Ice and packed ice are 0.98 there, blue ice 0.989, **slime 0.8**"* and the body returns only the three ice values; `SlimeBlock` falls to `kDefaultSlipperiness = 0.6`. The block exists, is craftable (`Recipe.cpp:886`) and already has a bounce (`Player.cpp:842`), so this is a value that was researched, written down and never wired. Bug shape #14 — a rule that did not travel. · confidence: **certain**
- **`Block.hpp:6058` `blockLightEmission(SeaPickle)` returns a flat 6** · Bedrock is 6/9/12/15 for 1/2/3/4 pickles **and 0 when not waterlogged**. There is one `SeaPickle` id with no count state, so the count half needs new ids; the waterlogged half is free, because `Chunk.hpp:75` `waterloggedAt` already exists and sea pickle is a Cross block, so it can already be waterlogged. A dry sea pickle currently glows. · confidence: **certain** · [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sea_Pickle](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sea_Pickle)
- **`Block.hpp:6088` `blockLightEmission(Glowstone)` returns 14** · Glowstone is **15** in both editions; 14 is the torch's value. Nether block, so one line and move on — but it is a one-character fix and the `static_assert`-free area around it is why nobody caught it. · confidence: **certain** · [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Light](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Light)
- **`Block.hpp:6064` `blockLightEmission(CrimsonFungus)` returns 6** · Crimson fungus emits **0**; it is grouped in an `if` with `SculkCatalyst`, which is correctly 6. Nether block, one line. Reads like a `||` added to the wrong branch. · confidence: **likely**
- **`Block.hpp:6335` `isSkyTransparent` includes `BlockShape::Model`** · That makes a chest, barrel, cauldron, anvil, hopper, campfire, bell, brewing stand, enchanting table, composter, grindstone and stonecutter all pass sky light at *full strength*, so a floor built of chests casts no shade at all. The listed justification covers fences, walls, gates and trapdoors (thin geometry) and does not obviously extend to a near-full cube. · confidence: **worth checking**
- **`Block.hpp:6299` `isLightTransparent` is `Air | fluid | Fire | isCutout`** · `isCutout` (`Block.hpp:2951`) has grown to include doors, trapdoors, anvils, hoppers, the monster spawner, scaffolding and the enchanting table for *rendering* reasons. Light transparency now rides on a rendering predicate, so widening `isCutout` for an art reason silently changes lighting. That is bug shape #2 with a rendering predicate as the family. Worth splitting into two predicates before it bites. · confidence: **worth checking**
- **`isFlammable` returns true for every `BlockShape::Cross`** · which includes `Kelp`, `SeaPickle`, coral plants and coral fans. Fire cannot exist underwater so it is harmless for burning, but **`blastResistance` uses `isFlammable` as its fall-through for "the woods, at 2.0"**, so kelp and coral get a wood's blast resistance instead of ~0. Same predicate, two consumers, one of them wrong. · confidence: **likely** · *(Citations made symbolic 2026-08-19: `Block.hpp:6381` was a bare number into a 12,519-line file, and `Explosion.cpp:436` was past the end of a 222-line file **and** the wrong file — `blastResistance` is a `constexpr` table in `Block.hpp`, not in `Explosion.cpp`, which reads it once in its intensity loop and says so in a comment. Grep the two function names.)*
- **`Block.hpp:6404` `feedsEternalFire`** names `Netherrack`, `MagmaBlock`, `SoulSand`, `SoulSoil` · In the reference, **magma block does not sustain eternal fire** (netherrack, soul sand and soul soil do — the last two only for soul fire). A magma block in the overworld will therefore hold a permanent flame. · confidence: **worth checking** · [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire)
- **`World.cpp:679–683`, the random-tick filter** · Not a bug so much as a hazard: the filter is a positive list, so every future ticking block must remember to add itself here *and* implement its rule. This is the "second place for the identical bug" shape (#10). Replacing it with a `ticksRandomly(BlockId)` predicate in `Block.hpp` beside `isFalling` puts the question in the block table where the rest of the answers live. · confidence: **certain** (design observation, not a defect)
- **`Block.hpp:6241` `canWaterlog` `static_assert`s** · `static_assert(canWaterlog(TallGrass) && canWaterlog(Kelp))` and `static_assert(!canWaterlog(StoneSlab) && !canWaterlog(CobbleStairs0) && !canWaterlog(Stone))`. The second one asserts the *current narrow policy* rather than a derivation, so it will fire the moment G6.5 is done — which is correct behaviour for an assert, but whoever does G6.5 should rewrite it to assert "a full opaque cube never waterlogs" rather than deleting it. · confidence: **certain**
- **`Farming.hpp:124` `kRandomTicksPerChunkPerTick = 8`** · Verified correct and worth recording so nobody "fixes" it: 32³ = 32,768 cells ÷ 8 samples = 4,096 ticks × 50 ms = **204.8 s mean per cell**, which is Bedrock's figure exactly. It is only right *because* `Chunk::kSize = 32` (`Chunk.hpp:18`); the two numbers are coupled and nothing asserts it. A `static_assert(Chunk::kBlockCount / kRandomTicksPerChunkPerTick == 4096)` would make that permanent. · confidence: **certain**

## 7. Survival and progression systems

**Scope:** Health, hunger, damage, hazards, status effects, armour, combat resolution, difficulty, death and respawn, sleep, fishing, freezing, fire, game modes — and the experience/enchanting/anvil chain that turns "staying alive" into "getting stronger". Overworld only.

**Headline verdict, revised 2026-08-19 09:57:** The *survival* half is genuinely finished and unusually faithful — twenty hearts, the hidden saturation buffer, exhaustion-driven hunger, the half-second invulnerability window with Bedrock's overwrite rule, every contact hazard on one shared cadence, a 33-item food table proved consistent at compile time, and 26 status effects on Bedrock's own numbering with Bedrock's own formulas. **✅ And armour, which this paragraph twice called the cheapest big win, is now closed** — worn, summed, reducing on every combat path, wearing down, and saved at player format version 7; what is left of it is a durability table, a HUD row and an equip sound. The *progression* half is close to zero. **There is no experience system of any kind** — no orbs, no levels, no bar, no furnace bank — and that single absence transitively blocks enchanting, the anvil, the grindstone, Mending and every gear upgrade past the smithing table; **with armour gone it is now the only large item in this section.** *Superseded: "Worse and cheaper to fix: armour is inert. All twenty-four pieces carry correct Bedrock defence and toughness values in `Item.hpp`, and nothing in the codebase calls either function."* One more system is built but unreachable — the grindstone (aliased to the anvil's repair); brewing was closed when `BrewingStand` joined `isInteractive`. There is no difficulty setting, no fishing, no shield, no freezing, no phantoms, no death messages, and no game-mode concept beyond a boolean creative flag.

> ✅ **The brewing half of that verdict is out of date.** `BrewingStand` is a term of `isInteractive`
> today, so all 41 brews and their four delivery forms are reachable. Everything else in the paragraph
> above still stands, including every word about armour.

**Completeness estimate:** roughly **40% → ~44%** of Bedrock's overworld survival and progression systems — call it **95%** of the survival half (85% when this was written; absorption, the golden apples' real effect sets, Slow Falling and the shared damage window landed on 2026-08-18) and under 10% of the progression half, which did not move at all.

> ✅ **What closed on 2026-08-18, and what pointedly did not.** Closed: the brewing stand is in
> `isInteractive`; Haste, Jump Boost and Slow Falling are read (`miningSpeedScale`, `jumpScale`,
> `fallSpeedScale`, the last corrected to Bedrock's 0.125); **Absorption is a real pool** on the player,
> granted only through `Effects::apply` so a spent pool cannot refill itself, dying with the effect
> rather than carrying into the next one; both golden apples grant their full published effect sets,
> held by `static_assert`s against the wiki's own figures; and **creatures joined the player's rules** —
> fall damage with Bedrock's two exception lists, suffocation, and the same `tickDamageWindow` /
> `chargeDamageWindow` pair rather than a second copy of the half-second window.
>
> **Not closed, and the first is now the only remaining item of its size in this section:** there is no
> experience system. ✅ **Armour closed 2026-08-19** — `armourDefence`/`armourToughness` are summed by
> `Inventory::armourSet`, spent by `survival::armourDamageTaken` inside `damagePlayer`, reached from
> combat because `Main.cpp`'s `hurtPlayer` takes a non-defaulted `ArmourSet`, worn down through
> `wearArmour`, and saved at player format version 7. **What is left of armour is small:**
> `mining::toolProperties` has no durability row for any of the 24 pieces so a set never breaks, there
> is no equip sound, and the HUD has no armour bar. ✅ **Absorption's HUD row landed 2026-08-18** —
> gold hearts on the line above the health row, drawn from `Player::absorption` — so the effects
> display is what is left of G7.24.
