### 7.3 Gap detail

#### G7.1 — Armour worn and reducing damage · L · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** Since **BE 1.18.30** Bedrock uses Java's non-linear formula, toughness included — the old flat 4%/point Bedrock model is history only. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Armor](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Armor)

  ```
  damageTaken = damage × ( 1 − min(20, max(armour/5, armour − 4×damage/(min(toughness,20)+8))) / 25 )
  ```
  Equivalently, reduction% = `min(80, max(0.8×armour, 4×armour − 16×damage/(toughness+8)))`, and the **breaking point** — the damage above which toughness stops mattering — is `armour × (toughness + 8) / 5`.
- **What we have, re-measured 2026-08-19 09:57:** ✅ **all of it except durability, the bar and a sound.** `armourDefence` and `armourToughness` (`item/Item.hpp`) hold the correct tables; `Inventory::armourSet` sums them across four slots and **refuses a piece sitting in the wrong slot**; `survival::armourDamageTaken` is the formula above, held by `static_assert`s at 30-through-full-diamond = 13.2 and 10-through-full-iron = 6.0; `damagePlayer` spends it; `Main.cpp`'s `hurtPlayer` takes a non-defaulted `ArmourSet` so combat reaches it; `wearArmour` charges `armourDurabilityCost`; `SavedPlayer::armour` persists the set at player format version 7. *Superseded text: "`armourDefence` (`Item.hpp:1513`) and `armourToughness` (`Item.hpp:1533`) with the correct tables, and no caller… armour cannot be equipped even in principle."*
- **What must be built — five of the six original items are done:**
  1. ~~Four equipment slots on `Inventory`, with `armourSlot(item)` deciding placement.~~ ✅ Done — `kArmourSlots = 4` beside the 36, `equipArmour` derives the destination from `armourSlot` so no caller can put boots on a head.
  2. ~~Four slots drawn in `InventoryScreen` and saved by `WorldStore`, needing a `player.dat` version bump.~~ ✅ Done — `slotAt` produces `SlotHit{Region::Armour, i}`, `build` draws the column, and the bump was spent: **player format version 7 is v6 plus the absorption clock and the worn armour**.
  3. ~~A single reduction applied inside `damagePlayer` so there is one owner.~~ ✅ Done, and better than proposed: the owner is `survival::armourDamageTaken` and `damagePlayer` is its only spender.
  4. ~~The **bypass list**, which is the half that gets forgotten.~~ ✅ Done and worth reading before touching it: reduced — melee, projectiles, explosions, lightning, falling anvils, and the contact hazards `Player.cpp` passes a real set for (fire, lava, magma, cactus); **not** reduced — magic/instant damage (a Harming potion passes `kNoArmour` at an explicit call site, because Bedrock routes it through `magic`), suffocation, drowning, starvation, the void. ⚠️ **Fall damage is unreduced here and that is unsourced** — `chargeFall` passes no set; nobody has checked Bedrock. Do not "fix" it from memory (`CLAUDE.md` bug shape #9).
  5. **Armour bar in `StatusBars` — still absent**, and no longer blocked by anything. `StatusValues` has no armour field. See G7.8.
  6. ❌ **New, and the only functional gap left: armour can never break.** `mining::toolProperties` has a durability row for every tool and for the bow and **not one row for any of the 24 pieces**, so a set wears (`wearArmour` runs, `ItemStack::damage` climbs) and then simply never reaches zero — a full diamond set is permanent free protection. **The numbers are already in the row below this one**, so this is a table edit, not research. Also missing: **no equip sound of any kind** — the reference plays `item.armor.equip_leather`/`_iron`/`_diamond`/`_netherite`/`_generic` the moment a piece goes on, and it is most of what makes equipping feel like it happened.
- **Numbers that matter:** points per piece (helm/chest/legs/boots): leather 1/3/2/1 (7), gold 2/5/3/1 (11), chainmail 2/5/4/1 (12), iron 2/6/5/2 (15), diamond 3/8/6/3 (20), netherite 3/8/6/3 (20); turtle helmet 2. Toughness: diamond 2 per piece (8 set), netherite 3 per piece (12 set), everything else 0. Netherite adds 1 knockback resistance per piece (10% each, 40% set). `armour` attribute caps at 30, `toughness` at 20. **Our tables already match all of this**, proved by `fullSetDefence`/`fullSetToughness` `static_assert`s rather than by reading. **Durability per piece — this is the table item 6 above needs:** leather 55/80/75/65, gold 77/112/105/91, chainmail 165/240/225/195, iron 165/240/225/195, diamond 363/528/495/429, netherite 407/592/555/481, turtle shell 275.
- **Risks / dependencies:** none left. The `player.dat` bump that was "the only migration risk" has been spent and verified. What remains is a durability table, a HUD row and a sound event.

#### G7.2 — Experience · XL · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Experience](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Experience)
- **What we have:** nothing. `Recipe.hpp`'s `repairResult` doc comment (line 116 as of 2026-08-19; the `:123` this replaced was past the end of a 120-line file) says so in a comment ("neither of which exists here"), and `RESEARCH.md` §10.4 is flagged **ACTIVE — not built**.
- **What must be built:** see the ordered programme in §7.4.
- **Numbers that matter:**

  *Level curve (edition-neutral — the wiki does not split it):*
  ```
  XP for the NEXT level:   2·L + 7      (L =  0–15)
                           5·L − 38     (L = 16–30)
                           9·L − 158    (L = 31+)

  Cumulative XP to reach L: L² + 6L                  (L =  0–16)
                            2.5L² − 40.5L + 360      (L = 17–31)
                            4.5L² − 162.5L + 2220    (L = 32+)

  Level from total XP:      sqrt(T + 9) − 3                      (T ≤ 352)
                            8.1 + sqrt(0.4·(T − 195.975))        (T = 353–1507)
                            18.0556 + sqrt((2/9)·(T − 753.0))    (T ≥ 1508)
  ```
  Anchors: L15 = 315 total, L16 = 352, L30 = **1395**, L31 = 1507, L40 = 2920.

  *Orb tiers (11, not 10):* 1, 3, 7, 17, 37, 73, 149, 307, 617, 1237, **2477**. A total is split highest-first (1000 → 617 + 307 + 73 + 3). Attraction radius **7.25 blocks**; pickup **10 orbs/s = 1 per 2 ticks**; despawn **6000 ticks / 5 min**; orb hitbox `[BE]` **0.25 × 0.25** (Java 0.5); same-value orbs merge without compounding. `[BE]` orbs appear only once the death animation finishes (20 ticks), not with the loot.

  *Drops:* passive animals 1–3 · babies 0 · most hostiles (zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider, drowned, husk, stray, enderman, witch, pillager, vindicator, phantom, silverfish, cave spider) **5**, plus 1–3 per equipment piece not dropped · guardian/evoker 10 · ravager 20 · slime 4/2/1 by size · breeding **1–7** · fishing **1–6** (one orb, at the player) · bottle o' enchanting **3–11** · villager trade 3–6. **A mob must die within 100 ticks (5 s) of player-caused damage to drop any XP.**

  *Ores:* coal 0–2 · redstone 1–5 · lapis 2–5 · diamond 3–7 · emerald 3–7 · monster spawner 15–43. **Iron, gold and copper give 0** — their XP comes from smelting. Silk Touch suppresses ore XP entirely.

  *Smelting (fractional, banked):* iron/copper ore + raw iron/copper + redstone ore **0.7** · gold ore/raw gold/diamond ore/emerald ore **1.0** · all raw food + potato + clay block **0.35** · logs 0.15 · stone/sand/cobble/coal ore/kelp **0.1** · lapis ore 0.2. The furnace **accumulates** it in a hidden counter, pays out only on manual collection (a hopper drains items and leaves the XP), awards the integer part and treats the remainder as a probability, and drops the whole bank as orbs if broken.

  *On death:* `7 × level`, **capped at 100** — so the cap binds from level 15 upward. `keepInventory` keeps XP too. Level resets to 0.
- **Risks / dependencies:** an XP orb is a new entity kind. `ItemEntity` already gives the pattern (physics, pickup box, 5-minute despawn — though see G7.19 note on despawn), so this is a copy rather than an invention. Everything downstream (enchanting, anvil, grindstone, Mending, the bar) waits on it, which is why it is XL and P0 despite delivering little on its own.

#### G7.3 — The brewing stand cannot be opened · XS · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** right-clicking a brewing stand opens it. (Our brewing is already a *named divergence*: instant, no fuel, no 20-second timer — that decision stands.)
- **What we have:** `Block.hpp:2824-2829`:
  ```cpp
  constexpr bool isInteractive(BlockId id) {
      return id == BlockId::CraftingTable || id == BlockId::SmithingTable || isFurnace(id) ||
             isChest(id) || isHopper(id) || id == BlockId::Grindstone || id == BlockId::Anvil ||
             id == BlockId::Stonecutter ||
             id == BlockId::ChippedAnvil || id == BlockId::DamagedAnvil;
  }
  ```
  It is the **only** caller-side gate (`Main.cpp:4374-4375`), and it omits `BrewingStand`. The branch at `Main.cpp:4413` that sets `openBench = BrewingStand` is therefore **unreachable**, and so are the brew paths at `Main.cpp:2923` and `3497` and every one of the 41 recipes behind them.
- **What must be built:** add `|| id == BlockId::BrewingStand` to `isInteractive`. Then verify by opening one — this is exactly the family-predicate bug shape from `CLAUDE.md`'s opening box, and the reason to *check every caller* rather than assume.
- **Numbers that matter:** none. One term.
- **Risks / dependencies:** none. Highest value-per-character change in the fragment.

#### G7.4 — Enchanting table · L · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Enchanting_table_mechanics](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Enchanting_table_mechanics)
- **What we have:** a block with a model, a texture and a name. No interaction path at all.
- **What must be built:** the table screen (item slot + lapis slot + three offer rows), the offer generator, the selection algorithm, the enchantment set on the stack, and a per-enchantment effect hook in the six places that read gear (mining speed, melee damage, arrow damage, damage reduction, durability spend, drop tables).
- **Numbers that matter:**

  *Bookshelf power:* max **15**. A shelf counts if it sits exactly 2 blocks out along one horizontal axis (up to 2 along the other), at table level or one block above. **`[BE]` divergence: the whole 2-high gap between shelf and table must be air** — a torch, a carpet or snow cover breaks it. (Java only checks one block, and uses a tag.)

  *Offer levels:*
  ```
  xpBase = 1 + randInt(7) + floor(min(15,shelves)/2) + randInt(min(15,shelves))
  top    = floor(max(1, xpBase/3))
  middle = floor(2·xpBase/3) + 1
  bottom = floor(max(xpBase, 2·shelves))
  ```
  With 15 shelves: top 2–10, middle 6–21, bottom exactly 30.

  *Cost:* lapis 1/2/3 by row. **You must *have* the displayed level but you are only *charged* levels equal to the lapis count** — a level-30 enchant costs 3 levels and 3 lapis. Item must be unenchanted. If the roll lands outside every valid range the item comes out plain **and no levels are taken**.

  *Selection:*
  ```
  eCost = round( (xpCost + 1 + randInt(⌊ench/4⌋) + randInt(⌊ench/4⌋)) × (1 + randTri(0.15)) )
      randTri(n) = (randFloat() + randFloat() − 1) × n     // triangular, not uniform
  loop: pick a candidate by weight; remove it and everything incompatible with it;
        stop if a (eCost+1)/50 roll fails; else eCost ← ⌊eCost/2⌋ and repeat.
  books: if more than one enchantment was selected, a random one is dropped.
  ```

  *Enchantability:* gold armour 25 · **gold tools 22** · leather / netherite / wooden tools / mace 15 · iron tools 14 · copper tools 13 · chainmail 12 · diamond (all) 10 · **iron armour 9** · turtle shell 9 · copper armour 8 · stone tools 5 · **book, bow, crossbow, fishing rod, trident 1**.

  *Weights:* 10 — Sharpness, Protection, Efficiency, Power, Piercing. 5 — Unbreaking, Fire Prot, Projectile Prot, Feather Falling, Knockback, Smite, Bane of Arthropods, Quick Charge, Loyalty. 2 — Aqua Affinity, Respiration, Blast Prot, Depth Strider, Fire Aspect, Looting, Fortune, Flame, Punch, Luck of the Sea, Lure, Impaling, Riptide, Multishot, Mending. 1 — Thorns, Silk Touch, Infinity, Channeling, Frost Walker, both curses.

  *Incompatibility groups:* {Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods} · {Fortune, Silk Touch} · {Protection, Fire Prot, Blast Prot, Projectile Prot} · {Depth Strider, Frost Walker} · {Infinity, Mending} · {Multishot, Piercing} · trident: Riptide excludes Loyalty and Channeling (Loyalty + Channeling are compatible).

  *Effects, Bedrock values:*
  - **Protection family (unified EPF model, both editions since BE 1.18.30):** EPF per level — Protection 1, Fire/Blast/Projectile Protection 2, Feather Falling 3. Sum the EPFs, **cap at 20**, reduction = `EPF/25`, **max 80%**, applied *after* armour points. No random component. So Protection is 4%/level, the three specialists 8%/level, Feather Falling 12%/level. Fire Protection also cuts burn time by 15%/level (7 total levels = fireproof).
  - **Sharpness `[BE]`: `floor(1.25 × level)` → +1/+2/+3/+5/+6.** (Java is `0.5L + 0.5`.) Smite and Bane of Arthropods `[BE]`: `floor(2.5 × level)` → +2/+5/+7/+10/+12. Bane also applies Slowness IV for 1–1.5 s at I, up to 3.5 s at V.
  - **Efficiency: `level² + 1` added to mining speed** (+2/+5/+10/+17/+26), and `[BE]` **only when the tool is the correct, harvest-capable tool**.
  - **Unbreaking:** tools/weapons `P(spend) = 1/(level+1)` → 50%/33.3%/25%; **armour `P(spend) = 0.6 + 0.4/(level+1)`** → 80%/73.3%/70%. Rolled per durability point.
  - **Fortune:** `P(no bonus) = 2/(level+2)`; otherwise uniform over 2..(level+1) multiplier. Average `1/(level+2) + (level+1)/2` → 1.33× / 1.75× / **2.2×**. Discrete-uniform blocks (redstone, glowstone, melon) instead get **+1 to the maximum per level**.
  - **Silk Touch:** the block itself, **no XP**.
  - **Mending: 2 durability per 1 XP point**; one randomly chosen damaged equipped item per orb, **no priority order**; leftover XP goes to the bar; XP does not reach the bar at all while any Mending item can absorb it.
  - **Respiration:** +300 ticks (15 s) of air per level over the base 300, so III = 1200 ticks (60 s); plus `level/(level+1)` chance per second to skip drowning damage (III = 75%).
  - **Aqua Affinity `[BE]`: all levels identical** (Java scales per level).
  - **Thorns `[BE]`: primary on helmet, leggings and boots as well as chestplate.** Each piece independently rolls `15% × level` to deal 1–5 damage, and costs 2 extra durability when it fires.
  - **Depth Strider:** +⅓ water-movement efficiency per level; III swims at walking speed. **Frost Walker `[BE]` freezes a *square* radius `2 + level`** (Java uses a circle).
  - **Looting:** +1 to max common drops per level, +1 percentage point to rare/equipment drop chance. **No effect on XP.**
  - **Power:** `25% × (level + 1)` arrow damage, rounded up to the half-heart → full-charge 6 becomes 9/11/12/14/15. **Punch:** +3.507 blocks at I, +3.3 per level after. **Flame:** 100 ticks (5 s) of burning, 5 HP total. **Knockback:** +2.586 blocks per level over a base 1.552.
  - **Luck of the Sea / Lure:** see G7.11.
  - **`[JE]` only — flag and skip: Sweeping Edge.** It has no Bedrock numeric id and the sweep attack does not exist in Bedrock at all.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.2 and G7.5. The effect hooks are the sprawl, not the table — this is where "give the answer one owner" matters: `breakSeconds`, `strike`, `damagePlayer` and the drop path must each read one enchantment accessor, not grow their own.

#### G7.5 — Per-stack enchantment storage · M · P0

- **Bedrock behaviour:** an item stack carries a list of `(id, level)` pairs plus a repair-cost counter.
- **What we have:** `ItemStack` is `{ ItemId item; int count; int damage; }` (`Item.hpp:1578-1590`). **`damage` is already overloaded** — for a stowbox it names which contents the box is carrying (`Item.hpp:1976-1981`, `Main.cpp:5815-5816`), which is why `maxStackFor` forces a stowbox to 1. So `damage` cannot be reused again, and the collision risk the brief flags is real.
- **What must be built:** a new fixed-size field on `ItemStack` — a `std::uint32_t` bitfield or a small `std::array<std::uint8_t, 4>` of `(id, level)` pairs; do **not** reach for a heap list, per the plain-data rule. Every site that copies a stack must copy it: `Inventory::add` (which takes `damage` as a parameter today — `Inventory.hpp:39`), `SlotOps.cpp:19`, `ItemEntity.cpp:74, 195`, `Main.cpp:2772` (chest save), `WorldStore` for both `player.dat` and the chunk block-entity payload. Both save formats need a version bump.
- **Numbers that matter:** Bedrock enchantment ids 0–41 fit in 6 bits; max level is 5, which fits in 3. Four `(id, level)` pairs is 36 bits — round to 5 bytes or two `uint32_t`. Bedrock's anvil work-penalty counter needs 5 more bits (`2^c − 1`, refused past 39).
- **Risks / dependencies:** the widening itself is the danger — `CLAUDE.md`'s rule about grepping for old literals when you widen what something can be applies exactly here, because nothing changes type and the compiler cannot help. A `static_assert` on `sizeof(ItemStack)` and on the round-trip through `WorldStore` is the cheap guard.

#### G7.6 — Anvil, properly · M · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Anvil_mechanics](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Anvil_mechanics)
- **What we have:** `repairResult` (`Recipe.cpp:1365`) — durability of both plus 5%, free, on a shared two-input bench.
- **What must be built:** the third input concept (rename field), enchantment merging, the cost model, the refusal, and anvil degradation.
- **Numbers that matter:**
  - **Total cost** = prior-work penalty of *both* items + 1 level if renaming + 2 levels if repairing + the enchantment cost.
  - **Prior-work penalty** = `2^c − 1` for use count `c` → 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31. The result takes the **higher** of the two inputs' counts, plus one.
  - **`[BE]` enchantment cost is dramatically cheaper than Java's:** Java adds `finalLevel × multiplier`; **Bedrock adds `(finalLevel − initialLevelOnTarget) × multiplier`**. Wiki worked example: a sword taking Sharpness III + Looting III from another sword costs **16 in Java and 1 in Bedrock**.
  - **Multipliers (from item / from book):** Protection, Sharpness, Efficiency, Power, Piercing, Loyalty 1/1 · Fire Prot, Feather Falling, Projectile Prot, Smite, Bane, Knockback, Unbreaking, Quick Charge, Impaling `[BE]` 2/1 · Blast Prot, Thorns→8/4, Respiration, Depth Strider, Aqua Affinity, Fire Aspect, Looting, Fortune, Punch, Flame, Luck of the Sea, Lure, Frost Walker, Mending, Riptide, Multishot 4/2 · Thorns, Silk Touch, Infinity, both curses, Channeling 8/4.
  - **"Too Expensive!" at > 39 levels** in Survival and Adventure. The wiki does **not** flag any Bedrock difference here — treat as shared. Creative removes the cap.
  - **Sacrifice repair:** target + sacrifice durability + **12%** of max (note: the *grindstone and crafting grid* bonus is **5%** — do not conflate; our `repairResult` correctly uses 5% and is therefore a grindstone/grid repair, not an anvil one). **Unit repair:** 25% of max per material unit, 1 level each, max 4 units.
  - **Rename:** 1 level; **`[BE]` max name 30 characters** (Java 50).
  - **Degradation: 12% per use** (not 25%) — average survival **25 uses**, σ ≈ 13.5. Three states, then destroyed with no drop. Falling >1 block: `5% × blocks fallen` chance to degrade a stage. **Falling anvil damage: 2 HP per block after the first, capped at 40 HP**; a helmet takes double durability and gives 25% reduction. A falling anvil entity drops as an item after 600 ticks (30 s).
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.2, G7.5.

#### G7.7 — Grindstone · S · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** removes all enchantments **except curses**, **resets the prior-work penalty to 0**, **keeps the custom name**, costs nothing, and **drops XP** when the output is taken. Repair is durability sum **+5%**, output always unenchanted, name and trim inherited from the top slot. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Grindstone](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Grindstone)
- **What we have:** `Main.cpp:4410` routes the grindstone to the anvil's screen and `repairResult`. The 5% repair is already right; the disenchant half does not exist.
- **What must be built:** a separate bench result for `BlockId::Grindstone` (the screen is already shared and parameterised by `openBench`, so this is one branch), enchantment stripping, and the XP payout.
- **Numbers that matter:** **XP dropped = a uniform random value between 50% and 100% (rounded up) of the summed *minimum modified enchantment levels* of all non-curse enchantments.** Sharpness V averages 35 (75% of 45). Reference minima: Sharpness 1/6/12/17/**23** · Efficiency 1/6/11/16/**21** · Protection 1/6/12/17 · Unbreaking 3/7/11 · Mending **13** · Fortune 8/12/17 · Silk Touch **8** · Looting 8/12 · Power 1/6/11/16/21.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.2, G7.5.

#### G7.8 — Armour bar and XP bar · S · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** armour bar is 10 icons / 20 half-points and **does not show points above 20**. XP bar sits under the health and hunger rows with a **green level number above it**; in Bedrock that Java-style layout requires the **Classic UI Profile** (mobile default puts health+armour top-left, hunger+oxygen top-right). Both bars are hidden in Creative. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display)
- **What we have:** `StatusValues` (`StatusBars.hpp:16-32`) carries health, food, air and hurt flash. Creative already hides the lot (`Main.cpp:2958-2962`).
- **What must be built:** two more fields on `StatusValues` and two more rows in `makeStatusBars`, plus the level number as text. The air row's `AirRow` pattern — a pure function that answers both "what is drawn" and "has anything moved" — is the model to copy for the XP bar's rebuild trigger, and for the same reason: a fraction comparison will otherwise leave the bar a frame late.
- **Numbers that matter:** 10 icons per row, half-units, as `kIconsPerRow` already has it.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.1, G7.2.

#### G7.9 — Difficulty · M · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** four settings; Bedrock's default is **Normal**, set per world at creation and changeable later. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Difficulty](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Difficulty)
- **What we have:** nothing. Normal is baked in — `Survival.hpp:127` ("Normal difficulty stops at one point... which is the difficulty we have"), `Player.cpp:378`, `Creature.cpp:2151`. `RESEARCH.md` §2.7 is marked OUT OF SCOPE and holds the scaling table.
- **What must be built:** a `Difficulty` enum in `Settings`, threaded to (a) hostile spawning, (b) mob damage, (c) the starvation floor, (d) lightning fire.
- **Numbers that matter:**
  - **Peaceful:** no hostile spawns and existing hostiles despawn; **no hunger loss and health regenerates regardless of food**; `[BE]` sleeping fully restores health on Peaceful only.
  - **Starvation floor:** Easy stops at **10 HP**, Normal at **1 HP**, Hard **kills**. (Ours is Normal's — correct, and `kStarveFloor` is already the one knob.)
  - **Mob damage scaling from the Normal value D:** Hard ≈ `1.5 × D`, Easy ≈ `min(D, 0.5D + 1)`. **Mob-versus-mob damage is always the Normal value.**
  - Zombies break doors on Hard; zombie reinforcements on Normal and Hard; villager→zombie-villager conversion 0% / 50% / 100% by Easy/Normal/Hard; **spider potion effects are `[JE]` only**; raid waves 3/5/7. **Lightning starts fires only on Normal and Hard.** Phantom group size 1–2 / 1–3 / 1–4.
  - Bedrock creeper explosions are ~35% weaker than Java's (14.75 / 27.5 / 41.25 by difficulty vs 22.5 / 43 / 64.5).
- **Risks / dependencies:** touches `Creature.cpp` in many places; the discipline is one `difficultyScale(kind)` accessor rather than a per-species branch.

#### G7.10 — Shields and blocking · M · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** `[BE]` a shield is raised by **sneaking** while it is held (Java holds use). 5-tick (0.25 s) activation delay, **100% reduction of blockable damage**, a 180° semicylindrical arc that **ignores pitch**, durability 336, and a 100-tick (5 s) disable when an axe strikes it. `[BE]` **Knockback still applies through a raised shield** (Java's does not), and since `[BE] 1.21.120` Punch knockback no longer does. Piercing arrows ignore shields entirely. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Shield](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Shield)
- **What we have:** the item and the recipe. No off-hand slot, no block input, no arc test.
- **What must be built:** an off-hand slot (or, cheaper, allow the shield to block from the main hand while sneaking, which is closer to Bedrock's control anyway), a raised flag with the 5-tick delay, an arc test against the incoming damage direction inside `damagePlayer`, and a durability spend of `max(1, damage)` when the blocked hit is ≥ 3 HP.
- **Numbers that matter:** as above. Durability spend only fires for blocked damage ≥ 3 HP.
- **Risks / dependencies:** `damagePlayer` currently takes only an amount; blocking needs a direction, so the signature grows. Add it once, at the one owner.

#### G7.11 — Fishing · M · P1

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fishing](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fishing)
- **What we have:** the rod item (`Item.hpp:1002`) and its recipe (`Recipe.cpp:390`). Nothing else.
- **What must be built:** a bobber projectile (our `Projectile.cpp` already has the species-table pattern), the wait timer, the bite window, three loot tables, and the catch XP.
- **Numbers that matter:**
  - **`[BE]` rod durability 385** (Java 64 — a genuinely surprising split, stated twice on the wiki). Durability spent **on reel-in**: nothing caught 0, successful catch 1, bobber stuck in a block 2, reeling a dropped item 3, reeling any other entity 5.
  - Bobber gravity **−0.03/tick²**, drag **0.92**. Line breaks past **32 blocks** (hooked entities at 33).
  - **Wait: uniform 100–600 ticks (5–30 s).** **Lure subtracts 100 ticks (5 s) from *both* bounds per level** → Lure III is 0–300 ticks. If it goes negative a new wait is rolled next tick.
  - **Rain reduces the wait ~20%** (each tick has a 25% chance to count down 2 instead of 1) — the 25% is the per-tick probability, not the net effect. **No sky above ≈ doubles** the wait (50% chance not to decrement). Both together ≈ **+33.3%**.
  - Bite: the particle trail runs **20–80 ticks (1–4 s)**, then the bobber dips. **`[BE]` reel window ≈ 10 ticks (0.5 s)** — Java's is 20–40 ticks. Miss it and the wait restarts.
  - **Categories: fish 85% / junk 10% / treasure 5%.** Luck of the Sea shifts to 84.85/8.08/**7.07** (I), 84.69/6.12/**9.18** (II), 84.54/4.12/**11.34** (III) — about +2.1 pp treasure and −1.95 pp junk per level. **Lure does not change the category odds.**
  - **Fish:** cod 60%, salmon 25%, pufferfish 13%, tropical 2%. `[BE]` jungle biomes reweight to 60/40/13/2 out of 115.
  - **`[BE]` treasure (differs from Java's flat sixths):** enchanted book 6/31, bow 5/31, fishing rod 5/31, name tag 5/31, nautilus shell 5/31, saddle 5/31. Enchanted bows/rods roll as a level 22–30 table enchant with 0–25% durability left. **Lily pad moved out of treasure into junk in `[BE]` 1.21.80.**
  - **`[BE]` junk (out of 101):** lily pad 17, then bone / bowl / leather / leather boots / rotten flesh / tripwire hook / water bottle at 10 each, stick 5, string 5, fishing rod 2, ink sac ×10 2. Junk rods and boots are 0–90% damaged and never enchanted.
  - **`[JE]` only — flag it: the open-water rule.** The 5×4×5 volume test that gates treasure is documented as Java-exclusive and no Bedrock page states an equivalent. Since Bedrock is our reference, **skip it** — but say so in a comment, because it is exactly the kind of rule a later session would "fix" from the Java page.
  - **XP: 1–6, one orb, spawned at the player, awarded on reel-in even if the catch is not picked up.**
- **Risks / dependencies:** the catch XP needs G7.2; everything else can ship first and simply drop no orb.

#### G7.12 — Armour durability and the enchantment layer · S · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** armour loses `max(1, floor(damage/4))` durability per absorbed hit, rolled against Unbreaking **per point**. Netherite armour is not damaged by fire sources.
- **What we have:** tool and bow durability only.
- **What must be built:** one call in the armour reduction path.
- **Numbers that matter:** the 1-per-4-HP rule; per-piece maxima listed in G7.1; Unbreaking's armour-specific `0.6 + 0.4/(level+1)` spend chance.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.1, G7.4.

#### G7.13 — Bedrock has no saturation healing · XS · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** natural regeneration is **1 HP every 80 ticks (4 s) while food ≥ 18**, costing **6.0 exhaustion per point healed**, and that is the whole of it. The fast path — 1 HP every 10 ticks (0.5 s) at full food costing 1.5 saturation — is tagged **`{{exclusive|java}}`** on the wiki. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Food](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Food)
- **What we have:** both paths. `Survival.hpp:132-134` defines `kSaturatedRegenInterval = 0.5f` and `kSaturatedRegenCost = 1.5f`, and `Player.cpp:354-369` runs the fast path whenever food is 20 and saturation > 0.
- **What must be built:** either delete the fast path, or — better, given the design here — keep it and mark it a **named divergence** in `Survival.hpp` alongside the brewing one. Deleting it is more faithful; keeping it makes cooked meat feel meaningfully better than bread, which is a real gameplay argument. Decide once and write down which.
- **Numbers that matter:** at 20 food with saturation, ours heals 10 hearts in 10 seconds; Bedrock takes 80 seconds and 15 food. That is an eight-fold difference in the most-used mechanic in the game.
- **Risks / dependencies:** none, but it interacts with G7.9 (Peaceful regenerates regardless of food).

#### G7.14 — Fire spread and ignition · M · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Fire)
- **What we have:** `BlockId::Fire` exists and renders; `isFlammable` exists (`Block.hpp:6396`); flint and steel is craftable and does nothing. No ignition, no spread, no extinguish.
- **What must be built:** flint and steel placing fire, the random-tick spread, the burn-out, and rain/water extinguishing.
- **Numbers that matter:**
  - **`[BE]` fire runs on random ticks and obeys `randomTickSpeed` (BE default 1)**; Java uses scheduled 30–40 tick ticks. This is a real divergence and Bedrock's is the simpler one for us — we already have a random-tick clock (`RESEARCH.md` §9.4).
  - Spread needs a player within 8 chunks. Per candidate cell: `degree = floor((i + 7d + 40) / (a + 30))` where *i* is the max adjacent burn-odds, *d* is difficulty 0–3, *a* is the fire's age. Base is 100 for the 3×3×3 neighbourhood, 200/300/400 for 2/3/4 blocks up. Probability = degree / base. **Halved in humid biomes** (jungle, swamp, mangrove swamp, snowy slopes, mushroom fields). Zero if rain hits the cell or any of its four horizontal neighbours.
  - Flammability (ignite / burn): logs and coal blocks 5/5 · planks and their stairs/slabs/fences 5/20 · bookshelf 30/20 · leaves and wool 30/60 · `[BE]` carpets **30/60** (Java 60/20) · hay bale 60/20 · `[BE]` 1-block flowers **30/100** (Java 60/100) · tall grass and 2-block flowers 60/100 · TNT and vines 15/100.
  - Age 0→15. Above age 3 with nothing flammable adjacent and no solid top below, it goes out next tick. At age 15 with nothing flammable below, ¼ chance per tick. **Rain: 20% + 3 percentage points per age → 20–65% per tick.**
  - Entity burning: **160 ticks (8 s) after leaving a fire block** — for players the counter starts at −20, so ≤1 s in fire costs nothing after you step out. Lava sets 300 ticks (15 s), refreshed every tick inside. **Our `kFireBurnSeconds = 8.0f` and `kLavaBurnSeconds = 15.0f` already match.** Fire Aspect adds `80 × level` fire-ticks, netting `(4 × level) − 1` HP because the first second is not counted.
  - `doFireTick` off: fire does not spread, destroy or extinguish — **but still burns entities**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** `mobGriefing`-style world options belong with G7.16.

#### G7.15 — Death messages · S · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** a message per cause, with a "whilst fighting/trying to escape X" variant for most. `[BE]` says *whilst* where Java says *while*. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Death_messages](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Death_messages)
- **What we have:** `engine::logInfo("Respawned.")` (`Main.cpp:4318`).
- **What must be built:** a `DamageSource` enum threaded through `damagePlayer` (which G7.10 needs anyway for the block direction), remembered as the last cause, and rendered on the death screen.
- **Numbers that matter:** the overworld set — *was pricked to death* (cactus) · *drowned* · **hit the ground too hard** (fall **< 5 blocks**) vs **fell from a high place** (**> 5 blocks**) · *fell off a ladder / some vines / scaffolding* · *was squashed by a falling anvil* · *was impaled on a stalagmite* · **went up in flames** (died *inside* a fire block) vs **burned to death** (on fire, not in one) · *tried to swim in lava* · *discovered the floor was lava* (magma block) · *was struck by lightning* · *froze to death* · *suffocated in a wall* · *starved to death* · *was poked to death by a sweet berry bush* · *blew up* / *was blown up by X* · *was slain by X* / *was shot by X* / *was impaled to death by X* · *was killed by magic* · *was killed trying to hurt X* (thorns) · *fell out of the world* · *died*.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the `DamageSource` parameter is the whole cost; share it with G7.10.

#### G7.16 — Game modes and world options · M · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Game_mode](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Game_mode) · [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Create_New_World](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Create_New_World)
- **What we have:** `bool creative` (`Main.cpp:2398`), read at ~25 sites.
- **What must be built:** a `GameMode` enum replacing the boolean (Survival / Creative / Adventure / Spectator), a Hardcore flag, and a world-options block in `Settings`.
- **Numbers that matter:**
  - IDs in `level.dat` `gametype`: Survival 0, Creative 1, Adventure 2, **Spectator `[BE]` 6** (Java 3), Default 5.
  - **`[BE]` Spectator is fully shipped** — non-experimental since **1.19.50**. Bedrock spectators cannot spectate *other entities* (that is Java-only). Fly speed 43.556 m/s, 87.111 sprinting.
  - **`[BE]` Hardcore exists** — added 1.21.0 preview, non-preview in **1.21.40**. It is a toggle that locks game mode to Survival and difficulty to **Hard**, disables Cheats / Starting Map / Bonus Chest, cannot be turned on for an existing world, and on death offers only "spectate the world" or exit.
  - Adventure gates breaking and placing on per-item `can_break` / `can_place_on` tags.
  - **Bedrock world-creation defaults:** game mode Survival, difficulty **Normal**, Hardcore off, show coordinates off, fire spreads **on**, mob loot on, natural regeneration on, tile drops on, skip night by sleeping on, immediate respawn **off**, simulation distance 4 chunks, cheats **off**, keep inventory **off**, mob griefing on, weather cycle on, **randomTickSpeed 1** (Java's is 3).
  - **`keepInventory = true` also keeps XP**, still resets health and hunger, still clears all effects, and does **not** destroy Curse of Vanishing items.
- **Risks / dependencies:** replacing the boolean is a mechanical but wide change; the `PlayerInput::invulnerable` design (`Player.hpp:230-234`) is already right — the physics never learns what a mode is — and should stay that way.

#### G7.17 — Freezing and powder snow · S · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powder_Snow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powder_Snow)
- **What we have:** the block, with correct break behaviour (`Mining.hpp` `miningRow`) and explosion handling. No entity interaction.
- **What must be built:** sinking, the freeze meter, freeze damage, the leather-boots exception and the vignette.
- **Numbers that matter:** `TicksFrozen` **+1 per tick inside, capped at 140 ticks (7 s)**; **−2 per tick outside**, so it drains in ~70 ticks (3.5 s). At full freeze, **1 HP every 40 ticks (2 s)** — i.e. 0.5 HP/s, *not* 2.5 hearts. Fire mobs take **5 HP per 40 ticks** instead. **Any one piece of leather armour stops freezing and reverses the meter.** Leather boots also stop you falling through and let you climb it like scaffolding. **All fall damage is negated** on landing in it, boots or not, and fall distance resets like water. It breaks instantly on contact with water, lava or a burning entity. Renewable source: a **cauldron under open sky in a snowy biome fills while it snows**. Movement inside is "much slower, similar to cobwebs" — **no numeric multiplier is published; could not verify.** Gamerule `freezedamage`.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the cauldron fill wants `Weather.cpp`'s precipitation answer, which already exists (`Weather.cpp:52`).

#### G7.18 — Bed rules and bounce · S · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** sleep needs internal sky light ≤ 11 — **ticks 12523–23477 clear, 12002–23998 raining, any time during a thunderstorm**. Refusals: **monsters within 8 blocks horizontally and 5 vertically of the bed head** (`[BE]` slimes and magma cubes count, piglins do not); "bed is obstructed"; **`[BE]` reach is 2 blocks** (Java 3). Sleeping runs **101 ticks (5.05 s)** before the skip; time goes to 0 (sunrise); **`[BE]` sleeping always resets the weather cycle** (Java only during rain/snow). Any damage wakes you. Falling onto a bed bounces at **75% of impact velocity and sets fall distance to 50%** — "slightly less than half of the normal fall damage", **not zero**. Missing or obstructed bed: "Your home bed was missing or obstructed", respawn at world spawn **and the point is cleared** — which our `Main.cpp:4310-4312` already does. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bed](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bed)
- **What we have:** respawn-point setting and the night skip (`Main.cpp:5449-5465`), with the point set day or night — correct. The skip is instant rather than 101 ticks, there are no refusal conditions, and the bounce is `kBedBounce = 0.66f` with `player.fallDistance = 0.0f` (`Player.cpp:851-856`).
- **What must be built:** the three refusal checks, the 101-tick hold, the weather reset, and the two bounce numbers.
- **Numbers that matter:** as above; the two corrections are **0.75 not 0.66**, and **halve the fall distance rather than zeroing it**.
- **Risks / dependencies:** the monsters-nearby check needs a creature query by box, which `Creatures` already supports for lightning (`Creature.hpp:1305`).

#### G7.19 — Absorption and Health Boost are inert · XS · P2

- **Bedrock behaviour:** Absorption grants 4 extra points per level, taken first and never regenerated; Health Boost raises maximum health by 4 per level.
- **What we have:** `effects::absorptionPoints` exists (`Effects.hpp:348-351`) with **no caller**, and Health Boost has no function at all — it is an enum entry and a colour. Both are applicable via `Effects::apply`, so a future source would silently do nothing. Neither has a brew today, so nothing is currently broken *in play*; this is a trap laid for the next system that adds one (a golden apple, notably, grants Absorption in the reference — and `foodValue(GoldenApple)` already exists at `Survival.hpp:169`).
- **What must be built:** an absorption pool on `Player` consumed before health in `damagePlayer`, a `maxHealth()` that reads Health Boost, and the extra half-hearts drawn by `StatusBars` (`StatusValues::maxHealth` is already a field and is already never assigned — see §7.5).
- **Numbers that matter:** 4 points per level, both effects. Absorption points do not regenerate and are lost when the effect ends.
- **Risks / dependencies:** none.

#### G7.20 — Phantoms and insomnia · M · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** the counter is **72000 ticks (3 in-game days)** since last rest, reset by **entering a bed or dying** — the wiki tags the Bedrock figure `{{verify|It seems to be longer in Bedrock}}`, so **the exact BE threshold is unverified**. `[BE]` spawn rules differ sharply from Java's: light level ≤ 7, subject to the monster cap, **density cap of 5**, attempts made on *surface* blocks in the normal spawn radius, and on success the phantom appears in a **21×15×21 cube centred 28 blocks above the player** — which means **`[BE]` phantoms can spawn in daylight**. Group size 1–2 / 1–3 / 1–4 by difficulty. Health 20 HP. **`[BE]` damage 4 / 6 / 9 by difficulty — three times Java's 2/2/3.** Swoops every 10–20 s. Drops 0–1 phantom membrane and 5 XP. Burns in sunlight; cats and ocelots repel them past 16 blocks. Gamerule `doinsomnia`. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Phantom](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Phantom)
- **What we have:** the membrane item (`Item.hpp:250`) and a trade row (`Recipe.cpp:1250`). No species, no counter.
- **What must be built:** a `ticksSinceRest` counter on the player saved in `player.dat`, reset at the two events, and a flying species. `RESEARCH.md` §7.2 already holds the flying archetype.
- **Numbers that matter:** as above. Flag the 72000 as unverified for Bedrock in the code comment.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.9 for group size and damage.

#### G7.21 — Trident · M · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** melee **9 HP** (crit 13.5), thrown **8 HP**, Channeling ranged total 13 HP. **`[BE]` durability 251** (Java 250). Cannot be crafted. **6.25% of naturally-spawned drowned carry one**; killed by a player or tamed wolf it drops at **8.5%, +1% per Looting level**. `[BE]` converted drowned never carry one. Projectile gravity −0.05, drag 0.99, not slowed by water. `[BE]` thrown tridents **do not despawn** (Java: 60 s) and can hit multiple entities. **Riptide launches `(6 × level) + 3` blocks in rain or standing water, `(4 × level) + 3` underwater** → 9/15/21 blocks at I/II/III; it needs rain on your block or water at your feet. **`[BE]` Impaling applies to everything in water *or rain*** (Java: aquatic mobs only), at `floor(2.5 × level)`. Loyalty return speed ≈ 0.83 blocks/tick per level. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trident](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trident)
- **What we have:** the item (`Item.hpp:1000`), no drowned trident-carrier, no throw.
- **What must be built:** a thrown-trident projectile (the `Projectile.cpp` species table is the right home), the drowned drop, and the four enchantments.
- **Risks / dependencies:** G7.4 for the enchantments; without them a trident is a slightly better sword.

#### G7.22 — Achievements and statistics · L · P3

- **Bedrock behaviour:** Bedrock uses **Achievements**, not Java's advancement tree — **133 achievements / 136 trophies**, 2,980 gamerscore, tracked **per account and per platform, not per world**, and **permanently disabled for any world ever saved with Creative mode, a flat world, cheats, behaviour packs, experiments or a Marketplace template**. 17 categories; all but *Nether* and *The End* are overworld-scoped (~110 of 133). **Bedrock has no statistics screen at all** — that is Java-only. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Achievement](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Achievement) · [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Statistics](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Statistics)
- **What we have:** nothing.
- **What must be built:** a flat achievement table with trigger predicates, a per-save bitset, and a toast. Notably, **the "disabled by Creative" rule is worth *not* copying** — this is single-player with one user, and the rule exists to protect a leaderboard we do not have.
- **Numbers that matter:** examples with exact triggers — *Adventuring Time* visit 17 biomes; *Passing the Time* play 100 in-game days (≈33 real hours); *On A Rail* 500 m by minecart in one direction; *Chestful of Cobblestone* open a chest holding 1,728 cobblestone; *Rainbow Collection* all 16 wool colours cumulatively.
- **Risks / dependencies:** most of the fragment above; it is the capstone, not a starting point.

### 7.4 The XP programme

XP is absent, and it is the single largest hole in the project's progression. Everything below is ordered so that **each step compiles, runs and is playable on its own** — no step leaves the game in a state where a half-built system is visible but useless.

| Step | Build | What it unlocks | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **X1** | **`world/Experience.hpp`** — the level curve, the orb tier table, the split function. Header-only `constexpr`, single owner of every XP number, exactly as `Survival.hpp` is for health. Prove the three-branch curve with `static_assert`s at L15/L16/L30/L31/L32 against the published cumulative totals (315 / 352 / 1395 / 1507 / 1628) — a curve written from memory comes out inverted often enough that this project has a rule about it. | Nothing yet. It is the table everything else reads. | XS |
| **X2** | **XP on the player** — `int level`, `int points`, saved in `player.dat` (version bump). `addExperience(n)` and `spendLevels(n)`. Drop `min(100, 7 × level)` on death and reset to 0. | The number exists and persists. | XS |
| **X3** | **The XP bar** — two fields on `StatusValues`, one row plus the green level number in `makeStatusBars`. Copy `AirRow`'s "one pure function answers both what-is-drawn and has-it-moved" pattern for the rebuild trigger. | **Playable milestone: the bar fills.** | S |
| **X4** | **Orb entities** — a new entity kind beside `ItemEntity`: gravity, 7.25-block attraction, 10 orbs/s pickup, **6000-tick (5 min) despawn**, same-value merging without compounding. Bedrock's 0.25×0.25 hitbox. `[BE]` orbs appear only after the 20-tick death animation. | Orbs fly to you and the bar moves. | M |
| **X5** | **Sources, in one table** — mob kills (passive 1–3, most hostiles 5, +1–3 per undropped equipment piece, **only if a player-caused hit landed within 100 ticks**), ore mining (coal 0–2, redstone 1–5, lapis 2–5, diamond/emerald 3–7, iron/gold/copper **0**), breeding 1–7, fishing 1–6, bottle o' enchanting 3–11. One `xpFor(...)` per source family, never a literal at the call site. | **Playable milestone: everything you already do now levels you.** | M |
| **X6** | **Furnace XP bank** — a hidden accumulator per furnace, paid out on manual collection only, integer part awarded and the fraction taken as a probability, remainder retained, whole bank dropped as orbs if the furnace is broken. `world/Furnace.hpp` already has the per-block state to hang it on. | Smelting becomes a level source; the hopper/manual distinction becomes meaningful. | S |
| **X7** | **Per-stack enchantment field** (G7.5) — the storage change and both save-format bumps, with `sizeof(ItemStack)` and a `WorldStore` round-trip asserted. **No gameplay yet.** Do it as its own step precisely because it touches ten files and nothing else should be moving at the same time. | The prerequisite for X8–X10. | M |
| **X8** | **Enchanting table** — the screen, bookshelf power with `[BE]`'s both-layers-air rule, the `xpBase` offer generator, the lapis/level charge (have the level, pay the lapis count), and the weighted selection loop with the triangular ±15%. Start with the **six enchantments that need no new hook**: Efficiency, Unbreaking, Fortune, Silk Touch, Sharpness, Protection — each lands on code that already exists (`breakSeconds`, the durability spend, the drop path, `strike`, `damagePlayer`). | **Playable milestone: the biggest single feeling of progression in the genre.** Requires G7.1 for Protection to mean anything. | L |
| **X9** | **The rest of the enchantment list** — Power/Punch/Flame/Infinity on the bow, Looting, Fire Aspect, Knockback, Respiration, Aqua Affinity, Thorns, Feather Falling, Depth Strider, Frost Walker, the three specialist Protections. Add `[JE]`-only **Sweeping Edge** to a "deliberately absent" comment so nobody adds it later from the Java page. | Gear variety. | M |
| **X10** | **Anvil and grindstone** (G7.6, G7.7) — the prior-work penalty `2^c − 1`, **Bedrock's cheap `(final − initial) × multiplier` enchantment cost**, the 39-level refusal, rename, books, 12% degradation; and the grindstone's disenchant with its 50–100%-of-minimum-levels refund. | The full gear economy closes: enchant, combine, strip, re-roll. | M |
| **X11** | **Mending** — 2 durability per XP point, one randomly chosen damaged equipped item per orb, no priority, leftover to the bar, XP withheld from the bar while any Mending item can absorb it. | The endgame item loop. | S |

**Total: roughly XL.** X1–X3 are half a day and produce a visible bar; X4–X6 are the real entity work; X7 is the risky one and deserves to stand alone; X8 is the payoff.

### 7.5 Errors and inconsistencies noticed while reading

1. **`world/Block.hpp:2824-2829` · `isInteractive` omits `BrewingStand`, making `Main.cpp:4413` dead code and all 41 brews unreachable · confidence: certain.** `isInteractive` has exactly one caller (`Main.cpp:4375`) and it is the only gate on the screen-opening path, so `openBench` can never be set to `BrewingStand` and the brew branches at `Main.cpp:2923` and `3497` can never run. Textbook instance of `CLAUDE.md`'s bug shape #2 — a family predicate that did not grow with its family — and of #14, a rule that exists in one of the two places that need it.

2. ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-19, re-measured 09:57 — `armourDefence` and `armourToughness` now have real callers and armour reduces real damage.** *Was: "`item/Item.hpp:1513` and `1533` · zero call sites anywhere in `game/src` · certain. Twenty-four pieces of correct, sourced Bedrock data that never reduce a single point of damage."* Both are summed by `Inventory::armourSet`, spent by `survival::armourDamageTaken` inside `damagePlayer`, and reached from combat because `Main.cpp`'s `hurtPlayer` takes a non-defaulted `ArmourSet`. **Left standing as the lesson, because this row was rewritten three times in four hours:** the original grep-for-callers verdict was correct when written and false within the hour, and an intermediate correction that said "it has callers now" was *also* misleading, because the only callers were `constexpr` self-tests feeding `static_assert`s. **A call-site count is not a reachability proof — ask what the caller is.** That is `CLAUDE.md` bug shape #15's own false-positive class.

3. **`world/Player.cpp:336-340` · the sprint test infers sprinting from raw speed, so Speed and Slowness both corrupt the exhaustion charge · confidence: certain.** The test is `length(velocity.xz) > kWalkSpeed + 0.1f` (4.417 m/s), but `Player.cpp:622` multiplies the target speed by `effects::moveSpeedScale`. Under Speed I, **walking** runs at 4.317 × 1.2 = 5.18 m/s and is charged the sprint rate of 0.1 exhaustion per metre instead of zero; under Slowness II, **sprinting** runs at 5.612 × 0.7225 = 4.05 m/s and is charged nothing. Wrong in both directions. The player already carries the answer — `PlayerInput::sprint` combined with the food floor at `Player.cpp:593` — so the fix is to record the sprint decision rather than re-derive it from a number that another system also scales. This is bug shape #1: a value derived somewhere other than the one place that owns it.

4. **`world/Player.cpp:851-856` and `world/Player.hpp:51` · a bed cancels fall damage entirely; Bedrock halves it · confidence: certain.** The reference bounces at **75% of impact velocity and sets fall distance to 50%**, giving "slightly less than half of the normal fall damage". Ours uses `kBedBounce = 0.66f` and then `player.fallDistance = 0.0f`. The comment beside it says "the reference's own numbers", which is what makes this worth flagging — a number ported with the wrong provenance written next to it is bug shape #3.

5. **`world/Survival.hpp:132-134` and `Player.cpp:354-369` · the fast saturation-heal path is Java-only and we are on Bedrock · confidence: certain.** The wiki tags the saturation regeneration boost `{{exclusive|java}}`; Bedrock has only 1 HP per 80 ticks (4 s) at food ≥ 18. Ours heals eight times faster at a full stomach. `RESEARCH.md` §3.4's "Where we stand" lists "the saturated fast-regeneration path at half-second intervals" among the things *taken verbatim*, which means the divergence was introduced believing it was fidelity. Keep it or cut it, but name it either way. See G7.13.

6. **`world/Effects.hpp:348-351` · `absorptionPoints` has no caller, and Health Boost has no function at all · confidence: certain.** Both effects can be applied through `Effects::apply` and both silently do nothing. Nothing brews them today, so nothing is broken in play — but a golden apple in the reference grants Absorption, and `foodValue(GoldenApple)` already exists, so this is one feature away from being a live bug.

7. **`hud/StatusBars.hpp:19-22` · `StatusValues::maxHealth` and `maxFood` are never assigned by any caller · confidence: worth checking.** The comment says as much and treats it as deliberate ("nothing assigns these, so whatever is written here is what ships"). That is correct today and becomes wrong the moment Health Boost (item 6) or a difficulty-varying maximum lands.

8. **`Main.cpp:4409-4417` · the grindstone is aliased to the anvil and produces the identical `repairResult` · confidence: likely deliberate, worth revisiting.** In Bedrock the two are different tools: the anvil preserves enchantments and charges levels with a 12% repair bonus; the grindstone strips enchantments, resets the work penalty, refunds XP and gives 5%. Ours gives both the grindstone's 5% and neither's distinguishing behaviour, which makes one of the two blocks redundant. `Recipe.hpp:120-123` is honest about why.

9. **`item/Recipe.cpp:1365-1381` · `repairResult` accepts any two items of the same kind including enchanted ones, once enchantments exist · confidence: worth checking (forward-looking).** Today it cannot matter. Once G7.5 lands, this function silently discards enchantments — which is *correct* grindstone/grid behaviour and *wrong* anvil behaviour, and the two currently share it.

10. **`Main.cpp:4419` · any `isInteractive` block that falls through the chain opens a crafting table screen · confidence: worth checking.** Harmless now because the chain covers every member of the predicate, but it is a `default:` that returns a real value — bug shape #10 — and it will quietly swallow the next block added to `isInteractive` without its own branch. The brewing stand's absence from the predicate and this catch-all are the same failure from opposite ends.

11. **Unverified, stated for honesty:** whether rain extinguishes a burning player (Bedrock's does; `Player.cpp:312` extinguishes only on `inWater` and Fire Resistance) — I did not trace the rain query into the player update. Bedrock's exact insomnia threshold (the wiki itself flags 72000 ticks as unverified for Bedrock). Powder snow's movement multiplier (no numeric value is published anywhere). Bedrock's enchanting-seed reroll semantics (the wiki's seed section is Java-only throughout).

## 8. Transport, vehicles and riding

**Scope:** Everything between "the player walks" and "the player arrives" — boats, minecarts and the rail network, ridden animals (horse/donkey/mule/llama/camel/pig), saddles, leads and leash knots, and the traversal blocks that change how fast a body moves (ladders, vines, scaffolding, ice, slime, honey, cobweb, powder snow, water columns). Overworld only; striders and elytra are named once as dependencies and dropped.

**Headline verdict:** This is the largest entirely-absent system in the project and the estimate is not close to arguable — **there is no vehicle, no rideable entity, and no passenger concept anywhere in `game/src`.** Grepping the whole game tree for `ride`, `mount`, `passenger`, `vehicle`, `boat`, `minecart` and `saddle` returns a `Saddle` item id with no consumer, a `lead.png` texture, and a comment about a fence's drawn rails. What *is* here is unusually good raw material: all four rail families exist as 40 block ids with the reference's exact ten-shape state space, the horse, donkey, mule, llama, camel and pig all exist as species with collision boxes and gaits, `Saddle` and `Lead` are already items (and the lead already has the *current* Bedrock recipe), and three separate non-creature entity systems — drops, projectiles and falling blocks — establish a house style precise enough to build a fourth against without inventing anything. The gap is therefore not "research a system"; it is "write the passenger relationship once, then bolt five vehicles onto it". **The single highest-value item is the boat**, because the world already generates oceans and the only way across one today is swimming at 2.20 m/s against a 15-second breath meter — the sole case where a missing vehicle makes an entire terrain type unusable rather than merely slow.

**Completeness estimate:** **~4%** of Bedrock's overworld transport surface. Being generous: rails-as-blocks (~40 ids, drawn and craftable but inert), ladder/vine climbing, ice slipperiness, and the void pearl's teleport are the whole of it. Vehicles, riding, taming, leads and rail logic are 0%.
